en: The Nirvāṇa of Śiva, accompanied by the seed-syllable mantra.
Oṃ, salutations to the illustrious Gaṇeśa. [Now begins the Nirvāṇa-paddhati. In a pure place, [using] earth, ashes, and cow-dung...

One should bring the ritual materials to that ground which one intends to smear with water. Regarding those whose time of death has arrived for whom this rite of upward departure (*samutkramaṇa*) is not prescribed, I shall describe the final funeral rite (*anty-eṣṭi*) as taught by Śiva.
By performing this Śaiva initiation (*dīkṣā*), even for those who are merely initiates (*samayins*) and have reached the limit of impurity, [the status of] an *ācārya* and so forth arises.

One should clearly perform the funeral initiation (antyeṣṭi-dīkṣā) for all those who are eligible, even those situated at lower levels including their gurus, provided they have been impelled by the descent of power (śaktipāta). May the Great Flame of Mātrī be victorious, she who bestows the auspicious state of Śiva; by the touch of the fire of her sparks, evil is reduced to ashes.

[This is] the *sāt* [mantra]. Therein, first, the purification of the ground is performed with the Aghora-weapon mantra: *oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ prasphura (2) ghora ghorataratanurūpa caṭa (2) pracaṭa (2) kaha (2) vama (2) ghātaya (2) hūṃ (3) hraḥ phaṭ (3) aghorāstrāya namaḥ*.

Having performed the purification of the weapons (*astra-śodhana*) with this, one should sit in the *vīrāsana* posture and worship the seat (*āsana*) as follows: "Obeisance to the Seat of the Self" (*ātma-āsanāya namaḥ*), "Obeisance to the Power of the Foundation" (*ādhāra-śaktaye namaḥ*), and "Obeisance to the Lotus Seat" (*kamala-āsanāya namaḥ*). Then, having drawn three lotuses with vermilion or rice powder, one should worship the components of the seat within those three lotuses, beginning with the Foundation (*ādhāra*).

Having worshipped the set of seats with the following: "Oṃ Raśaktyai namaḥ," "Oṃ Pṛthivyai namaḥ," "Oṃ Kṣīrārṇavāya namaḥ," "Oṃ Bījāṅkurāya namaḥ," "Oṃ Unmanāya namaḥ," "Oṃ Padmāsanāya namaḥ," "Oṃ Pretāsanāya namaḥ," and "Oṃ Praṇavāsanāya namaḥ"; then, upon that worshipped seat, [one should place] a vessel filled with scented water, perceived through the vision of both duality and non-duality.

One should worship the three *la*s; having placed fruits and other offerings upon them, one should perform the worship. First, one should worship the *arghapātra* (offering vessel) for the weapon (*astra*) on one's own right side with: *oṃ gaḥ astrāya phaṭ*, *kaḥ astrāya phaṭ*, *raḥ astrāya phaṭ*, *yaḥ astrāya phaṭ*. With that [mantra], one says: *oṃ hūṃ phaṭ sarvadravyopacāraśuddhir astu phaṭ*.

Again, with their respective mantras: *Oṃ ādhūmra (2) jīva (2) saḥ saḥ, may the life-force of all species of flowers come, svāhā!*—for the flower. *Salutation to Kālāgnirudra in the form of incense, who is the fragrance of the world and the bearer of all scents!*—for the incense. *Salutation to him whose form is the light of the world!*—for the lamp. *To Gandhamādin, the life-force of fragrance!*—for the perfume.
*Payatu svāhā* for sandalwood (*candana*). *Oṃ hrīṃ saḥ* for saffron (*kuṅkuma*). *Oṃ lāṃ pṛthivyai dharitrī-śaktyai namaḥ* for the water-offering (*arghya*).

*Blīṃ varuṇa-rājānakāya namaḥ* for the water (*udaka*). *Yāṃ rāṃ lāṃ vāṃ* for all the most excellent substances (*sarvottama-dravyebhyaḥ*)—thus [one offers] to all the substances. This is the purification of the substances (*dravya-śuddhiḥ*). *Oṃ hūṃ*, with the *akṣita* mantra and others, I perform the binding of the directions (*dig-bandhanaṃ karomi namaḥ*).

This is the mantra for the binding of the ten directions (*digbandhana*). Then, with the *nārāca-mudrā* formed by joining the middle fingers and thumbs, immediately after the application of flowers, one should ward off the obstacles that disturb the celestial and atmospheric realms by striking with the *koṭikās* and three blows of the heels. Having done so, one should perform the binding of the ten directions with the *triśūla-koṭikās*.

Having displayed the mudrā, one should perform *prāṇāyāma* with the mantra: *oṃ pūrakaṃ 12 kumbhakaṃ 24 recakaṃ 36*. With the mantra *laṃ recakaṃ karomi namaḥ 12*, one should expel the purified vital air (*prāṇavāyu*) through the right nostril for the duration of twelve recitations of the *praṇava*. Then, with *vaṃ pūrakaṃ karomi namaḥ 24*, [one should inhale].

One should cause the pure white prāṇa-vāyu to enter within the left nostril for as long as it takes to recite twenty-four praṇavas, [saying]: "Raṃ, I perform kumbhaka; namaḥ" (36). One should restrain that very same prāṇa-vāyu within for as long as it takes to recite thirty-six praṇavas, maintaining an immovable state like a jar filled with water, [saying]: "Yaṃ ū..."

"Oṃ Ūrdhvarecakam karomi namaḥ. Having thus performed the *kumbhaka* (retention), one should slowly expel the breath through the left nostril by means of the sequence of piercing the heart, throat, palate, the space between the eyebrows, and the *brahmarandhra*, as it cannot otherwise be expelled. This is the *ūrdhvarecaka*. "Oṃ Haṃ, I establish the self as the nature of space; namaḥ. One should contemplate the subtle self situated within the heart-lotus, resembling a firefly, shimmering like a star.

Having projected the syllable *ka* through the sequence of piercing the heart, throat, palate, between the eyebrows, and the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*) up to the *dvādaśānta*, and having dissolved the mind (*manas*), ego (*ahaṅkāra*), and intellect (*buddhi*) into the Supreme Reality (*paratattva*), one should meditate upon the body as empty; this is the purification of the subtle body (*sūkṣmaśarīra*). Then, one should perform the purification of the gross body (*sthūladeha*) through the meditative concentrations (*dhāraṇā*) of drying and so forth, [reciting]: "Kṣyūṃ! Obeisance to that which dries up this body. Thus, one's own...

One should contemplate the body as having the form of a withered tree; this is the Earth [element]. Then, reciting "ṚKṢŪM, I burn this body, namaḥ," one should meditate on the Fire of Time (Kālāgni) rising from the big toe of the right foot and imagine the body, both internally and externally, reduced to ashes by its flames;
this is the Fire [element]. Then, reciting "YLŪM, I cause the body to float upward, namaḥ," one should [dispel] the bodily ashes with the wind. This is the Air [element].

"One should meditate on [the wind] pervading the directions"—thus is the Vāyavī [mudrā]. With the mantra "Vaṃ, I bathe the body; obeisance," one should meditate on that place being washed by streams of nectar flowing from the *cidbindu* (point of consciousness) situated at the *dvādaśānta* (the limit of twelve finger-breadths above the head)—thus is the Vāruṇī [mudrā].

Just as the harmfulness of poison is warded off by the power of a mantra, so too the identification with the body (*dehāhaṃbhāva*) is dissolved by the power of the mantra; it is not the destruction of its essential nature (*svarūpa*). Thus it is said.
[This is] the state of being.
Thus, when the body consisting of the six sheaths has ceased, one should contemplate the Self as consisting of supreme bliss: "Oṃ, I am the pure *haṃsa*;
I am not this [body], nor is there anything else here; and no object of meditation exists here, for I am absorbed in the state of bliss."

Having attained the state of mental equanimity (*samarasīgata*), the practitioner of the space-element (*ākāśī*) should then place the seat (*āsana-pakṣa*) starting from the *kanda* up to the heart, reciting:

*oṃ ādhāraśaktyai namaḥ*, *kṣīrodārṇavāya namaḥ*, *candramaṇḍalāya namaḥ*, *padmāya namaḥ*. Just as [the breath] was led upward by the upward exhalation (*ūrdhva-recaka*), so too by the upward inhalation (*ūrdhva-pūraka*) [one reaches] the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*), the middle of the eyebrows, and the palate.
Having projected the self into the heart-lotus by way of the throat, one should say: *oṃ juṃ saḥ tanvaṃ amṛtīkaromi namaḥ*.

Having thus bathed [the body] with streams of nectar flowing from the *cidbindu* at the *dvādaśānta*, it is revived. Then, saying *oṃ māyādikṣityanta-ekatriṃśattattvarūpāya śuddhadehāya namaḥ*, the pure body is produced.
One should meditate. Then: "Obeisance to Brahmā; obeisance to Vāstupuruṣa; obeisance to the one whose form is *haṃ*."

Then, in the case of the door-deity and the water-pot (kalaśa), the lotus-worship is as follows: "Obeisance to the Halo" (prabhāmaṇḍalāya namaḥ), "Obeisance to the Bull" (vṛṣabhāya namaḥ), "Obeisance to Bhṛṅgīśa" (bhṛṅgeśāya namaḥ), "Obeisance to Kumāra" (kumārāya namaḥ), and "Obeisance to Ambikā" (ambikāyai namaḥ). Now, the worship of the door (dvārapūjā).
Laṃ, obeisance to Indra, who holds the thunderbolt in his hand. (10) Then follows the worship of the Mothers of the Directions in the order starting from the east.

*Namaḥ* to Nandin on one's own left; *namaḥ* to Mahākāla on one's own right; worship of Gaṇeśa in the northwest (*vāyu*); worship of Sūrya in the southwest (*nairṛta*); worship of Kumāra in the center; worship of the Planets (*graha*) on one's own right. Then, the ritual placement (*nyāsa*): *Oṃ hrāṃ* to the heart, *hrīṃ* to the head, *hūṃ* to the tuft of hair (*śikhā*), *hraiṃ* to the armor (*kavaca*), *hrauṃ* to the eyes, *hraḥ* to the weapon (*astra*). *Oṃ oṃ* *namaḥ* to the principle of the self (*ātmatattva*).
In the heart: *oṃ juṃ namaḥ* to the Vidyā-tattva; in the throat: *oṃ saḥ namaḥ* to the Śiva-tattva; on the head:
then the Nyāsa of the nine tattvas—*oṃ namaḥ* to the Śiva-tattva at the aperture of the crown (*karandhra*); *namaḥ* to the Sadāśiva-tattva on the forehead;
*namaḥ* to the Īśvara-tattva between the eyebrows; *namaḥ* to the Vidyā-tattva at the palate; *oṃ mā*... [at the root of the nose].

Salutation to the principle of *yāta* at the throat; salutation to the principle of *kāla* at the heart; *Oṃ*, salutation to the principle of *niyati* at the navel; *Oṃ*, salutation to the principle of *puruṣa* at the penis; *Oṃ*, salutation to the principle of *prakṛti* at the feet. Now, regarding the initiated person, [the mantras are]: Aghora, Aghorīśvarī, Niṣkala, Amṛtīśvara, and Amṛtalakṣmī.

Regarding the subject of initiation (*dīkṣita*), one should perform the six-limbed assignment (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) with this mantra. Thereafter, the assignment of the armor (*astrādinyāsa*) and so forth is performed in reverse order:

Oṃ haḥ, salutation to the weapon (*astra*) of infinite strength and power, phaṭ namaḥ. Oṃ hauṃ, salutation to the eyes (*netra*) of undecaying power, vauṣaṭ namaḥ. Oṃ haiṃ, salutation to the armor (*kavaca*) that is self-dependent, huṃ namaḥ. Oṃ hūṃ, [salutation to] primordial awakening (*anādibodhi*).

*Śikhāya evaṣaṭ namaḥ*. *Oṃ hīṃ tṛpti-śirase svāhā namaḥ*. *Oṃ hāṃ sarvajñatva-hṛdayāya namaḥ*. *Oṃ guṃ bahurūpa-bhairavāya vauṣaṭ*. *Guṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ*. *Guṃ śirase*. *Guṃ śikhāyai*. *Guṃ kavacāya*. *Guṃ netrebhyaḥ*. *Guṃ astrāya*. *Oṃ hrīṃ māyā-devyai namaḥ*. *Hāṃ ṣaḍ-aṅgāya*.

Then, one should perform the Śivahasta rite; joined with the five faces and established by Śiva, this Śiva is proclaimed as the Śivahasta, the cutter of bonds. [Recite: "Obeisance to the lunar orb" on the left hand, and "to the solar [orb]" on the right hand.

*Maṇḍalāya namaḥ*. Having sprinkled the palm of the right hand with auspicious water (*śivāmbhas*) and consecration water (*astrāmbhas*), and having performed the veiling (*ava-guṇṭhana*), one should perform the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) for the Deity and worship Him. Then, having applied the five-fold tilaka with *kṣaṃ yaṃ raṃ vaṃ laṃ*, [one recites]:
*kṣaṃ īśānavaktrāya namaḥ* (to the face of Īśāna), *yaṃ tatpuruṣavaktrāya namaḥ* (to the face of Tatpuruṣa), *raṃ aghoravaktrāya namaḥ* (to the face of Aghora).

[Recite] "Paṃ, obeisance to the face of Vāmadeva" [at the right], "Uṃ, obeisance to the face of Sadyojāta" [at the left], and in the center, "Obeisance to the face of Tatpuruṣa. Having performed the purification of the body and the vital breath (*prāṇa*) along with the limbs of worship,

and having placed the two hands upon the head, one should sprinkle them with water using the *astra-mantra*, veil them with the *kavaca-mantra*, transform them into nectar by means of the *amṛteśvarī-mudrā*, and drench them with that nectar.

Having prepared the six-limbed seat (*ṣaḍaṅgāsana*) with flowers placed in the other hand by means of the middle finger and thumb of that [other] hand, and having worshipped the root mantra together with its limbs and faces, one should place the left hand upon the right hand;
then, one should place the right hand on the heart and the left hand on the head. This is the ritual of the Hand of Śiva (*śivahastavidhi*). Then, the five...
The procedure for the *gavya* (cow-products): Having prepared nine squares with rice powder and having placed vessels together with seats within them,

one should place cow dung with the *hṛdaya-mantra* in the west, cow urine with the *śiras-mantra* in the north, curd with the *śikhā-mantra* in the east, milk in the center with the *varma-mantra*, ghee in the south with the *astra-mantra*, and water with *kuśa* grass in the northeast with the *netra-mantra*, in due order.
Having merged all these with the *mūla-mantra*, one should worship Śiva. Reciting "Oṃ haḥ phaṭ, I purify the vessels, phaṭ" seven times, he consecrates them with the water of Śiva (*śivāmbhas*).
Then, having encircled the vessels with the armor mantra (*kavaca*) by reciting "Haiṃ, I envelop the vessels, hūṃ," he proceeds from the central square in the sequence starting from the east.
One should worship up to the northeast (Īśāna) in the nine-fold principle-worship (*navatattvapūjā*). [The offerings are as follows: "Salutation to the Śiva-principle" in the center;
"Salutation to the Sadāśiva-principle" in the east; "Salutation to the Īśvara-principle" in front; "Salutation to the Vidyā-principle" on the right;
"Salutation to the Māyā-principle" in the southwest; "Salutation to the Kāla-principle" in the west; "Salutation to the Niyati-principle" in the northwest...

*Maḥ*: Homage to the Puruṣa-tattva in the northwest (*vāyu*). Homage to the Prakṛti-tattva in the north (*uttara*). And again in the northeast (*īśāna*), homage to Supratiṣṭhā. In the center, homage to Svaśāntā. In the east, homage to Tejovatī. In the south, homage to the one named Amṛtā. In the west, homage to Ratnodayā. In the north, [homage to] Gomayā; [one should apply] cow-dung with the *hṛdaya-mantra*.

Having recited *oṃ hāṃ* once for the heart, [one says]: *laṃ sadyojātamūrtaye namaḥ*; [place] cow dung, the size of a thumb, in the western directional vessel. For the head, in the north: *oṃ hrīṃ śirase svāhā*; having consecrated it twice, [say]: *vaṃ vāmadevaguhyāya namaḥ*; [place] one *pala* of cow urine in the north. In the east, [place] curd.
Having consecrated it three times with "Oṃ hūṃ, obeisance to the crest (śikhā),

vauṣaṭ," and [consecrated] four times with "Raṃ, obeisance to the heart of Aghora, namaḥ" in the east, and with "Oṃ haiṃ, obeisance to the armor (kavaca), hūṃ" in the center, [one should place] a piece of meat the size of a palm and milk in the middle while reciting the *varman* mantra.

Having consecrated [the substances] five times with the mantra "Oṃ haḥ phaṭ astrāya phaṭ," [one places] milk measuring one *pala* in the center, saying "Namaḥ to the face of Tatpuruṣa"; ghee in the south, saying "Namaḥ to Īśāna, the head," with the weapon-mantra;
and in the right eye, water from *kuśa* grass for the night, saying "Hauṃ vaṣaṭ to the eyes" and "Hūṃ namaḥ to Śiva," [with the ghee] measuring half a thumb's breadth.

"To that Maheśa," thus [reciting], one should offer a palmful of kuśa-water to Īśāna. Then, having placed each preceding substance in front of the one following it while uttering its respective mantra, one should combine the cow-dung and the other substances, ending with the milk. It is as follows: *Oṃ hāṃ lāṃ, I join the cow-dung, whose nature is nectar; Oṃ hīṃ vaṃ, I join the cow-urine, whose nature is the arising of jewels, [to this]—namas*. Oṃ...
Hīṃ vaṃ, I offer cow urine to the self whose nature is the arising of jewels; Oṃ hūṃ yaṃ, I offer curd to the self who is peaceful in nature—namas!
Oṃ hūṃ yaṃ saḥ, I join the self of peace in curd; oṃ haiṃ kṣaṃ, I join the self of perfect stability in milk; obeisance!

Oṃ haiṃ kṣaṃ: I join the milk, which is my own self established in the *ātmatattva*, with the ghee, which is like fire; oṃ haḥ raṃ: [I join] it, namaḥ. One should place the vessel of milk together with that [ghee] in kuśa-water by means of the root mantra. The *Īśvara-tattva* situated in the southeast [is joined] with the *Māyā-tattva* in the southwest. The *Māyā-tattva* situated in the southwest [is joined] with the *Niyati-tattva* in the northwest. The [Niyati-tattva] situated in the northwest...

One should pour *kuśa* water into the *prakṛti-tattva* located in the northeast (*aiśāna*). Then, one should place a lotus upon the fire located in the southwest (*nairṛta*). Having stirred it with the six-limbed mantra (*ṣaḍaṅga*), one should render it nectar (*amṛta*) by means of the *Amṛteśa-mudrā*. There, one should perform the worship of the seat (*āsana-pūjā*): "Oṃ, obeisance to the Seat; obeisance to the Support-Energy (*ādhāra-śakti*); likewise [obeisance] to Earth, to Milk..."

[The mantras] beginning with *praṇava*, *bījāṅkura*, *padmāsana*, *pretāsana*, *praṇava*, and *unmanā* [are used] regarding the initiated person, the *sakala-baṭṭāraka*, and so forth. Then, there is sprinkling (*prokṣaṇa*) with a seat of *darbha* grass over which the seven weapons have been recited;
again, there is sprinkling with the *nārāca-astra* mantra, and by that, one should display the *nārāca-mudrā*. *Oṃ nārācāstraṃ*.

One should meditate upon the remover of obstacles (Vighnahara), who resembles the sun, is fierce, has three blazing eyes, and holds a trident and a noose with his [characteristic] mudrā. Or, one may meditate upon him above the vessel; on the left is the shield (kheṭaka). One should worship Aghora and Aghorīśvarī along with their limbs (aṅgas), having visualized the earth as being filled with pearls. [With the mantra] "Haḥ Phaṭ," [one worships] the sword of knowledge (jñānakhaḍga), which consists of the thirty-six principles (tattvas).
"Oṃ, salutation to the water for the feet; salutation to the fragrant unguent for the body; salutation to the *arghya*; salutation to the flower.
Then, one should perform twelve purificatory rites (*saṃskāra*) with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*): Oṃ phaṭ, I perform the digging up, phaṭ (1);
Oṃ phaṭ, sprinkling (2); smearing (3); filling (4); pounding (5); wiping (6); sprinkling upwards (7).
Having performed the purificatory rites with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*), including (8) the extraction of the thorn and (9) the filling with pearls;

Now follows the worship of the conch (*śaṅkhapūjā*). *Khaḍgāya* and so forth, ending with *vajrāya phaṭ sarvam*. To the sword, the sharp, the cutter, the shatterer, the all-seeing great wheel-king, *svadhā*; to the one who causes fear to all the wicked, cut! split! swallow the mantras of others! break them! terrify them! *hūṃ phaṭ*! Homage to the wheel! To the conch!
"Obeisance to Yaṇamaḥ, obeisance to Saśarāya, obeisance to Kāmodakāya, obeisance to Mahābalāya;
obeisance to the fragrant unguent for anointing, obeisance to the water-offering (arghya), obeisance to the flower. Thus ends the worship of the conch. Now follows the worship of the bell.

I worship the messenger (Dūtī), who is gentle, four-armed, whose voice is her own, who utters mantras, and who holds in her hands a rosary, a book, a garland, and the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness. Oṃ hūṃ, to the messenger Śuddhavidyā, the mother of mantras; oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, to the messenger of Śiva, [offer] water for the face and water for the guest-offering. The mantra for sounding the instrument: oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ siddhasādhini oṃ hrīṃ.

HŪṂ, O you whose nature is the Sound-Brahman; OṂ HRĪṂ HŪṂ, O destroyer of all bonds; OṂ HRĪṂ HŪṂ, O awakening one; OṂ HRĪṂ HŪṂ, O mother who generates the true state of Śiva, SVĀHĀ. (50) OṂ HŪṂ, O Supreme Brahman, O fourfold knowledge, O bearer of yoga, O Self, O Inner Self, O Supreme Self, O power of Rudra, O beloved of Rudra, O consort of the Lord, burn away my sin, O ever-peaceful one! (2)
ŚIVE HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ. VIDMA (0) AMṚTĪŚVARĀYA VIDMA (0) (3), VIDMA (0) BAHURŪPĀYA VIDMA (0) (3). Thus ends the worship of the messenger (dūtī).

Then, on the lotus petals, beginning from the eastern petal and proceeding counter-clockwise, one should worship as follows: *Oṃ vāmāyai namaḥ*, *jyeṣṭhāyai*, *raudryai*, *kālyai*, *balavikariṇyai*, *balapramathinyai*, *sarvabhūtadamanyai*, *manonmanyai*.
Then, in the northeast (Īśāna), one should worship the Astra-kalaśa with: *Oṃ ślīṃ paśu hūṃ phaṭ*; *Oṃ hṛ* [namaḥ]; *ślīṃ śira* [namaḥ].

The *śikhā* [mantra] is: *sukava hūṃ netre phaṭ astrāya*. Now, the *aghorāstra*: *oṃ hrīṃ prasphura 2 ghoraghorataratanurūpa caṭa 2 pracaṭa 2 kaha 2 vama 2 ghātaya 2 hūṃ 3 hraḥ phaṭ 3 aghorāstrāya phaṭ namaḥ*. Then, the *codanāstra*: *hrīṃ hūṃ hraiṃ hraḥ codanāstrapādukābhyāṃ namaḥ*.

Oṃ, salutation to Khaḍga; [salutation to] Kheṭaka, Pāśa, Aṅkuśa, Śara, Pināka, Vara, Abhaya, Muṇḍa, Khaṭvāṅga, Vīṇā, Ḍamaru, Ghaṇṭha, Paraśu, and Mudgara. Oṃ, phaṭ to Vajra; phaṭ to Śakti; [salutation to] Daṇḍa and Khaḍga.

One should worship [the weapons] in the Astra-kalaśa with the following: "To the noose," "to the banner," "to the mace," "to the trident," "to the lotus," "to the plow," and so forth. Then follows the worship of the Śakti-kalaśa on the right: "Salutation to Vāmā" (2); then the Gāyatrī: "Tat maheśāya vi" (3); "Yamāntakāya vi" (3); "Agniṣṭhātebhyaḥ vi" (3); "Oṃ."

*Hrīṃ bhuvanamālinyai namaḥ*. Now, the *Kulamālinī* mantra: *Oṃ nṛḷḹ tha ca dhīṇu ū ba ka kha ga gha ṅ i a va bha ya ḍa ḍha ṭha jha ña ja ra ṭa pa cha la sā aḥ ha ṣa kṣa ma śa aṃ te a i o au u dha pha mālinyai namaḥ*. [Va] (0) (50). Other mantras...

Vāyana-maḥ. Its limbs are as follows: Oṃ namaḥ sarvātmane parameśvarāya yogāya yoga-sambhavāya kara kara sadya sadya bhava bhava bhavodbhava bhavodbhava vāmadeva sarvakārya-pramathana namas te svāhā. Oṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ. Oṃ śiva śiva namaḥ śirase namaḥ. Śivo hṛda.

To the crest of the sacrificial flame, Svāhā! Oṃ! You who are of the nature of Śiva, the great splendor, all-knowing, unconquered, the most formidable, the auspicious tawny armor—summon this armor! Come, O tawny Great Armor, by the command of Śiva! Bind the heart! Ghūrṇa (2) Kāki (2) Sūkṣma (2)!

Vajradhara! O Vajrapāśa, O Vajrāśani, enter my body; paralyze all malevolent beings, hūṃ phaṭ! O armor, hūṃ! Oṃ prasphura (2) sphura (2), you whose form is most terrible and fierce, naṭa (2) pracaṭa (2) karṣa (2) dhama (2) ghātaya (2) hūṃ phaṭ! O weapon, phaṭ!

Oṃ! This universe has Śiva as its essence; it proceeds from Śiva alone. For the sake of Śiva, for him who contains Śiva within his womb, may Śiva impel all things. (3) Oṃ! Īśāna is the lord of all sciences, the lord of all beings, the overlord of Brahman, the overlord of the Veda; may he be the eternal Śiva, Oṃ. Oṃ Aḥ Maḥ.
Gha-svāhā-phaṭ, to the heart; Oṃ pañcamūrtaye namaḥ, to the head; Oṃ īśāne svāhā, to the crest-lock; Oṃ jvalanti namaḥ phaṭ, to the armor; Oṃ hūṃ sadasadoṃ phaṭ, to the weapon, phaṭ.
To Tatpuruṣa we pay homage (vidmahe)—(3)—Oṃ tatpuruṣa sadasadoṃ, to the heart; Oṃ bhūḥ svāhā, to the head; Oṃ.

*Bhuvaḥ svāhā* for the *śikhā*; *Oṃ svaḥ svāhā* for the *kavaca*; *Oṃ tatsat oṃ* for the *astra*. The mantra *Oṃ aghorebhyaḥ...* [is used] for the heart (*hṛdaya*). *Oṃ tatsat oṃ* for the heart. *Oṃ bhava caṇḍa hūṃ phaṭ* for the head (*śiras*). *Oṃ bhīma-bhīṣaṇi sarva-vidyā-hṛdaya-vicāriṇi hūṃ phaṭ* for the crest-lock (*śikhā*). *Oṃ amogha hūṃ phaṭ* for the armor (*kavaca*).

Oṃ tatsat oṃ astrāya | Oṃ vāmadevāya namaḥ; to Jyeṣṭhā, to Rudra, to Kāla, to Kalavikaraṇa, to Balavikaraṇa, to Balapramathana, to Sarvabhūtadamanaka, and to Manonmanī. Oṃ vāmadeva tatsat oṃ hṛdayāya; vāmadevāya hūṃ phaṭ śirase; [to] Sarvapāpapraṇāśinī Vāmā.
*Devashikhāya namaḥ* for the crest (*śikhā*). *Vāmācārāya hūṃ phaṭ* for the armor (*kavaca*). *Tatsad om astrāya* for the weapon (*astra*).

*Oṃ sadyojātaṃ prapadyāmi sadyojātāya vai namaḥ | bhave bhave nātibhave bhajasva māṃ bhavodbhava ||* (I take refuge in Sadyojāta; salutations indeed to Sadyojāta! O source of existence, in every birth, in non-existence, and beyond existence, protect me, O source of being!)

Oṃ *sadyaḥ-kāmāya svāhā* (Heart); *sadyaḥ-kāma-vara-pradāya namaḥ namaḥ* (Head); *pannaga-rūpiṇe svāhā* (Crest-lock); *sadyaḥ-mūrtaye phaṭ* (Armor); *oṃ hūṃ oṃ phaṭ* (Weapon). Then [worship] Aghora, Aghorīśvarī, Niṣkala, along with their limbs (*aṅga*), faces (*vaktra*), weapons (*āyudha*), and retinues (*āvaraṇa*). Bhairava...

The armor: Oṃ guṃ to Bahurūpabhairava, vauṣaṭ. The limbs: guṃ to the heart (hṛdaya), guṃ to the head (śiras), guṃ to the crest-lock (śikhā), guṃ to the armor (kavaca), guṃ to the eyes (netra), guṃ to the weapon (astra). Oṃ hrīṃ to Māyādevī, vauṣaṭ. Hrāṃ: the six limbs. Then the mantra-circle: Gaṇeśa, Vallabhā, Kumāra, Sūrya, Visphurā, Amṛteśvara, Amṛta.

Lakṣmī, the six-syllabled mantra, Lakṣmī-Vāsudeva, obeisance to Viṣṇu, O Viṣṇu, Lord of Food; Bhagavatī, Kuleśvarī, Vāgīśvarī, Durgā, Vanadurgā, Gaurī, Siddhalakṣmī, Śārikā, Śāradā, Jyeṣṭhā, Yogīśvarī,
Ekāntī, Kubjikā, Caṇḍayogīśvarī, Vāgvādinī, Vitastā, and Annapūrṇā.

One should worship Lakṣmī, Vittalakṣmī, Viḍā, Mahārājñī, Jvālāmukhī, and Kālikā in this sequence within the Śakti-vase. Then, one should worship the Kṣetrapālas, beginning with Āmardaka, in order starting from the east: *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ āmardakāya namaḥ* (3), *Oṃ kaṅkālāya* (0), *Oṃ bhīmarā* (0).

(3) Aṭṭahāsa (3) Karavīra (3) Karaṅkākhya (3) Kāligrāsa (3) Kuleśvarāya namaḥ. Having offered the sacrificial food (*naivedya*) consisting of molasses and other items, one should place seven grains in this sequence. Then, having brought the disciple forward, one should cause him to perform worship. First, there is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*): Oṃ hṛ [heart], na śira [head], maḥ śikhā [crest-lock], vā netre [eyes], ya astra [weapon].

Oṃ hṛda (0), juṃ śiraḥ, saḥ śikhā, Amṛtīśvarāya kava, Bhairavāya netre namaḥ, astrā (0). Oṃ, obeisance to the Śivatattva at the aperture of the crown; Sadāśiva (0) on the forehead; Īśvaratattva between the eyebrows; Vidyātattva on the palate; Māyātattva on the feet. One should perform the Aghora-nyāsa and the others upon those who have been initiated.
Oṃ, I bow; we worship Maheśa. Oṃ Hrīṃ Saḥ, the purifier. To my own self, whose nature is Śiva:

homage for the fragrant unguent (samālambana), homage for the water offering (argha), homage for the flower. [To the one who is] the death of worldly existence, the fire of time, two-armed, to my own self, Śiva: [homage for] incense, lamps, and so forth. Now, for the weapon (astra), for the power (śakti), for the Śiva-vessel (śivakalaśa).

To the sacrificial deities; to Āmardaka, Kaṅkāla, Bhīmarāva, Aṭṭahāsa, Karavīra, Karaṅka, Kāligrāsa, and Kuleśvara—incense, svadhā, obeisance! Lamp, svadhā, obeisance! [With the sacred thread over the right shoulder] today, for the father, belonging to the Bhairava lineage, who is Rudra...
To Mātrebhairava-gotra and others, to Rudrāṇī and others, for the purpose of other desired rites: incense, *svadhā namaḥ*;
lamp, *svadhā namaḥ*. With the left hand: "We know that Great Lord" (0); (3) "to those [deities] in the fire" (0); (3) "to Yamāntaka" (0);
(3) now, of the weapon (*astra*), of the powers (*śakti*), of the deities of the Śiva-vessel (*śivakalaśa*) such as Āmardaka and others, and of oneself...

"I shall perform worship for the sake of other desired rites; Oṃ, do so!"—in this manner, proceeding in order until the end of the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), one then performs the worship of the jewel-lamp. With the right hand, [one recites] "Salutation to you, O Great..."; with the left hand (in the *apasavya* position), [one recites] "To Raktā, to Karālī, to Caṇḍākṣī, to Mahocchvāsā, to Karālinī, to Dantarā, to Bhīmavaktrā, to Ma..."

Homage to Hābalāya! Homage to Yamāntaka! Today, for the sake of increasing the radiance [of my] father in the other world, on account of the funeral rites (*antyeṣṭakarman*), and for the sake of attaining the state of Śiva, I offer this lamp;
homage! Today, on account of the funeral rites for my father Rudra of the Bhairava lineage...

Through the propitiation of the Astra-kalaśa, through the Śakti-kalaśa, and through the propitiation of the Śiva-kalaśa with sesame-water, may the Lords of the Field (Kṣetrapālas) be pleased; may they be pleased. Then follows the ritual bath for the deceased (Śava-snāna): ŚLĪM PAŚU HŪM PHAṬ (10), OṂ HRĪM HŪM (2), PRASPHURA (2), GHORAGHORATARATANURŪPA CAṬA (2), PRACAṬA (2), KAHA (2), VAMA (2), GHĀTAYA (2).

HŪṂ (3) HRAḤPHAṬ (3) AGHORĀSTRĀYA PHAṬ NAMOḤ | OṂ HRĪṂ HRŪṂ HRAIṂ HRAḤ CODANĀSTRĀYA PHAṬ NAMOḤ | ĀṂ ĪṂ ŪṂ VYOMAVYĀPINE NAMOḤ (10). Regarding those who are initiated: AMṚTEŚVARA, AMṚTALAKṢMĪ, AGHORA, AGHORĪŚVARĪ, NIṢKALA with its limbs, the weapons and the armor, and the Bhairavas.
The *varaṇa* (protection): *Oṃ laṃ sadyojāta-vaktrāya*, *Oṃ vāmadeva-vaktrāya*, *Oṃ raṃ aghora-vaktrāya*, *Oṃ yaṃ tatpuruṣa-vaktrāya*, *Oṃ kṣaṃ īśāna-vaktrāya*.
The assignment (*nyāsa*) of Bhairava is as follows: *Oṃ rthaṃ namaḥ* to the feet; *Oṃ yaṃ namaḥ* to the knees; *Oṃ vaṃ namaḥ* to the private parts;
*Oṃ laṃ namaḥ* to the heart; *Oṃ maṃ namaḥ* to the throat; *Oṃ kṣaṃ namaḥ* to the arms; *Oṃ raṃ namaḥ* to the mouth.

*Oṃ saṃ namaḥ* on the head; *oṃ haṃ namaḥ* at the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*). [Perform] the *niṣkala* [mantra] for each [limb]. Then, having propitiated [the deity] with the water from the three jars, reciting: *oṃ guṃ namo bahurūpabhairavāya* and *oṃ hrīṃ namo māyādevyai*, one should perform the placement of the Bhairava mantra (*bhairavamantranyāsa*) from the feet to the head, and then perform the placement of the syllables (*akṣaranyāsa*).
Just as *oṃ guṃ bahurūpabhairavāya ūṃ namaḥ* is for the feet, likewise: *oṃ guṃ yaṃ namaḥ* for the knees;
*oṃ guṃ vaṃ namaḥ* for the secret place; *oṃ guṃ laṃ namaḥ* for the heart; *oṃ guṃ maṃ namaḥ* for the throat;
*oṃ guṃ kṣaṃ namaḥ* for the arms; *oṃ guṃ raṃ namaḥ* for the face; *oṃ guṃ saṃ namaḥ* for the head; *oṃ guṃ haṃ namaḥ*.

In the *brahmarandhra*. Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) in this manner, one should perform the libation (*tarpaṇa*) upon that head: "I offer libation to Bhairava, together with his limbs and faces; *svadhā namaḥ*! Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, I offer libation to Manonmanī; I offer libation to Sarvabhūtadamanī;
I offer libation to Balapramathinī; I offer libation to Balavikariṇī; I offer libation to Kālī; I offer libation to Raudrī."

(3)ṃ Jyeṣṭhāṃ (0) (3)ṃ Vāmāntāṃ (0)—thus is the libation (*tarpaṇa*). Now, the Mālinī [mantra]: Oṃ nṛ ḷ ḷ tha ca dhī ṇu ū ba ka kha ga gha ṅa i a va bha ya ḍa ḍha ṭha jha ña ja ra ṭa pa cha la ā sa aḥ ha ṣa kṣa ma śa aṃ te a i o au da pha mālinyai namaḥ. The syllables (50).
One should worship that head three times with flowers and other offerings, reciting: *oṃ hūṃ bahurūpabhairavāya namaḥ* (three times).
Having offered libations (*tarpaṇa*) into the *arghya* vessel at the head, one should apply a forehead mark (*tilaka*) on the forehead with the fire-weapon mantra (*agnyāstra*), as follows:
*oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hraiṃ hrauṃ hraḥ phaṭ*. With this, one should apply the *tilaka*.
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, [reciting] "the sacred thread, obeisance," one should offer it beginning from the feet; then one should fasten the loincloth;

thereafter, one should bring forth the garments and perform the sprinkling (abhyukṣaṇa). Immediately after that, one should worship the desired mantras, along with their limbs (aṅgas) and faces (vaktras), upon the head. Then, one should perform the "Hand of Śiva" (śivahasta) rite for Śiva.

The ritual placement (*nyāsa*) on the limbs is as follows: *phaṭ astrāya phaṭ* [for the weapon], *jyoṃ netrābhyāṃ vauṣaṭ* [for the eyes], *hūṃ kavacāya hūṃ* [for the armor], *īṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ* [for the crest-lock], *vyoṃ śirase svāhā* [for the head], and *juṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ* [for the heart]. This is the ritual placement.
Then, the incense offering: *hrīṃ pare brahman caturvidhe yogadhāriṇi ātme antarātme paramātme*.
*Rudraśakti rudradayite, burn away my sin! O gentle Sadāśivā, hūṃ phaṭ!* Then, with the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra, one should sound the jewel-lamp and then the messenger: *Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ Siddhasādhini;
oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ Śabdasvarūpiṇi; oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ Samastabandhanikṛntini; oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ Bodhini; oṃ hrīṃ...*

HŪṂ ŚIVASADBHĀVAJANANI SVĀHĀ. PHAṬ! I sprinkle the betel in the mouth and the nine gates. PHAṬ! I perform the sprinkling. Then one should offer garments; having covered the face with a red cloth, one should recite the mantra: *so'haṃ saḥ, namaḥ śivāya*, [and] "O beloved Goddess"—thus is the essence of all.

Regarding the consecrated person, one should write the Aghora mantra with its limbs (sāṅga), the Niṣkala with its limbs, and the nine-syllabled Vyo-ma-vyāpin; this is the tradition of the Guru concerning the ritual bath of the instruments (karaṇasnāna).
Then, having adorned the corpse with garlands of skulls, one should smear its feet with honey and [place] grass...

"May the jars be without cracks"—thus ends the procedure for the bathing of the corpse. Now follows the worship of the palanquin (*śivikā*). Upon it, with three...

Sprinkling from the *arghyapātra* vessel: *Oṃ hūṃ phaṭ*, "I perform the sprinkling, phaṭ. Thus, there is sprinkling three times. Upon that, having spread *darbha* grass, one sprinkles again with sesame seeds using the *astra* mantra: *Hūṃ kavacāya hūṃ*; thus, the veiling (*avaguṇṭhana*) is performed with the *varma* mantra. Then, the worship of the three principles (*tritattva-pūjā*): at the crest-lock (*śikhā*), *Oṃ saḥ śivatattvāya namaḥ*.

Oṃ juṃ, obeisance to the Vidyā-tattva; Oṃ oṃ, obeisance to the Ātma-tattva—at the head. Now, the worship of the five tattvas: in the center, obeisance to the Ātma-tattva; [obeisance to] the Vidyā-tattva; [obeisance to] the Śiva-tattva; [obeisance to] the Prakṛti-tattva; [obeisance to] the Puruṣa-tattva. Now, the worship of the nine tattvas on the branches: obeisance to the Śiva-tattva—at the head; [obeisance to] the Sadāśiva-tattva.

[The assignment of the principles: Īśvara in the southeast (Agni), Vidyā in the south (Dakṣa), Māyā in the southwest (Nairṛta), Kāla in the west, Niyati in the northwest (Vāyu), Puruṣa in the north, and Prakṛti in the northeast (Īśāna). Then, in the middle and subsequently in the branches: "Obeisance to Niyati" and "to Kalā"; [and] the branches are:
Pratiṣṭhākalā, Vidyākalā, Śāntākalā, and Śāntātītākalā. Thus are the branches.
Then, in the middle of the palanquin, this should be written: *Hūṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ*. Next is the worship of the seat (*āsana-pūjā*):
*Namaḥ* to Ādhāraśakti; to Ananta; to the Earth; to the Ocean of Wine (*surārṇava*); to the Fragrance; to the Stem;
to the forms of its throat, the Vidyās and Vidyēśvaras; to the Seat of Knowledge (*vidyā-siṃhāsana*); to the Lotus; to Knowledge (*jñāna*); to Dispassion (*vairāgya*).
To fear, to sovereignty, to unrighteousness, to ignorance, to non-dispassion, to lack of sovereignty;

to the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda, the Atharvaveda; to the Kṛta age, the Tretā age, the Dvāpara age, the Kali age; to the lower covering, the middle covering, the upper covering; to the lotus, to its petals, and to its filaments.

To the pericarp: *namaḥ* to the solar disc (*sūryamaṇḍala*), the lunar disc (*somamaṇḍala*), and the fiery disc (*vahnimaṇḍala*). To the lords of the solar disc, Brahmā; to the lord of the lunar disc, Viṣṇu; to the lord of the fiery disc, Rudra; and to the qualities of goodness (*sattva*), passion (*rajas*), and darkness (*tamas*). Then, one should worship the five vessels (*pañcabhāṇḍī*).

Just as: *Vauṣaṭ* to the drum (*paṭaha*) for Brahmā; *vauṣaṭ* to the gong (*kāṃsyatāla*) for Viṣṇu; *vauṣaṭ* to the cymbals (*tūrya*) for Rudra; *vauṣaṭ* to the flute (*vaṃśa*) for Īśvara; *vauṣaṭ* to the drum (*muraja*) for Sadāśiva.
Then, having placed the corpse upon a palanquin (*śibikā*), one should offer the funeral cake (*piṇḍa*). [The mantra: *Śastra-cūrṇa-śārikā-bhru*.

One should throw *hilāja* and other substances before the corpse. (2) One should perform the purification of the path with water from the *astravāṭikā*. One should recite the *Bahurūpagarbha* mantra and the word "Victory" (*jaya*). They should carry the corpse to the cremation ground. Thus ends the ritual for the consecration of the corpse.

Now follows the ritual for the cremation ground (*śmaśāna*). Therein is the salutation to the cremation ground: Oṃ! Having firmly squeezed [the world] all around with both hands, having repeatedly resolved upon the entire cosmic egg (*brahmāṇḍa*) as a fruit fully ripened by the mind, and having repeatedly drunk the juices of the three worlds with intoxicated movements, he performs his eternal *tāṇḍava* dance.

"By means of the ritual of *ḍambare*, Mahābhairava [is propitiated] from calamity. Thus ends the salutation. Now, in the middle of the cremation ground (*śmaśāna*), one should cast a stream of flowers into the center. Having placed the corpse facing south and having sat upon one's own seat facing north, one should smear the ground and there, with vermilion or rice powder, draw three lotuses.

O King, having drawn an eight-petaled *muṇḍayāga* below that, and having fashioned a triangular fire-pit (*agnikuṇḍa*) to its south, one should write the *Māyājāla* in the southwest corner of the mental representation. One should perform the worship of the seats (*āsana-pūjana*) upon the three lotuses as follows: "Salutation to the Seat" (*āsanāya namaḥ*), "to the Support-Energy" (*ādhāraśaktyai*), "to the Earth" (*pṛthivyai*), and "to the Ocean of Milk" (*kṣīrārṇavāya*).

One should fill [the vessel] with scented water, saying: "Obeisance to the Seed-Sprout, to the Lotus Throne, to the Corpse Throne, to the Praṇava Throne, and to the Transmental (Unmanā). Then, having worshipped the General Arghya-vessel on one's right, [one recites]: *gaḥ astrāya phaṭ*, *kaḥ astrāya phaṭ*, *raḥ astrāya phaṭ*, *yaḥ astrāya phaṭ*, *astrāya phaṭ*. With that [water],...

*Phaṭ*, may there be the purification of all ritual substances, *phaṭ*. Again, with their respective mantras: *Oṃ ādhūmra (2) jīva (2) saḥ saḥ*, may the life-force (*jīva*) of all varieties of flowers come here, *svāhā*. For the flower: *Gandham ādine gandhaṃ jīvāpaya svāhā*. For the sandalwood: *Oṃ hrīṃ saḥ*. For the saffron: *Oṃ lāṃ pṛthivyai dhari*.

*Traśaktyai namaḥ* (Salutation to the power of trembling) for the *argha* offering. *Oṃ blīṃ varuṇarājānakāya namaḥ* (Salutation to Varuṇa, the King of Waters) for the water. *Oṃ kālāgnirudrāya jagaddhūpasugandhine sarvagandhavahāya dhūpāya namaḥ* (Salutation to Kālāgnirudra, who is fragrant with the incense of the universe and the bearer of all scents) for the incense. *Oṃ jagajjyotirūpāya svaprakāśātmane dīpāya namaḥ* (Salutation to the lamp, whose form is the light of the universe and whose nature is self-luminous) for the lamp. *Yāṃ rāṃ lāṃ vāṃ sarvottamadravebhyo namaḥ* (Salutation to the most excellent liquids).

This is the purification of all substances (*dravya-śuddhi*). Then, having performed the binding of the directions (*digbandhana*) with *phaṭ astrāya phaṭ*, one should display the trident mudrā (*triśūla-mudrā*) and perform breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) [in the ratios of] 12, 24, and 36 [breaths]. Then, one should worship the messenger (*dūtī*) as before, reciting the mantra.

Ṭhaṃ, the placement of the limbs: *Haḥ* to the weapon (*astra*) of infinite power, *phaṭ*; *Hauṃ* to the eyes of the one whose power is unceasing (*ananta-lupta-śakti*), *vauṣaṭ*; *Haiṃ* to the armor (*kavaca*) of the independent one (*svatantra*), *hūṃ*; *Hūṃ* to the crest (*śikhā*) of primordial awakening (*anādi-bodhi*), *vaṣaṭ*; *Hīṃ* to the head of contentment (*tṛpti*), *svāhā*; *Hāṃ* to the heart of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), *namaḥ*. *Yaḥ* to the weapon (*astra*), *phaṭ*; *Vāṃ* to the eyes, *vauṣaṭ*.

*Śikavacāya hūṃ maḥ*, *śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*, *śirase svāhā*, *oṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ*. One should perform other mantras for those who have received initiation (*dīkṣita*). Therein, one should perform the worship of three jars (*kalaśa*) as follows: first, one should worship the *astra-kalaśa* on one's own left with: *ślīṃ paśu hūṃ phaṭ paśupatāstrāya namaḥ*. *Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ pra...* [and so forth].

*Sphura* (2), *ghoraghorataratanurūpa-caṭa* (2), *pracaṭa* (2), *kaha* (2), *vama* (2), *ghātaya* (2), *hūṃ* (2), *hraḥ phaṭ* (3). Homage to the Aghora weapon! *Hrīṃ hrūṃ hraiṃ hraḥ*. Homage to the impelling weapon! Homage to the sword! (12 times). *Vajrāya phaṭ* (10 times). Having worshipped the vessel of weapons with these, then, to the right of oneself, perform the worship of the Śakti-vessel and the Fire-vessel. Or...

*Māyainam iti tanmaheśāya vidmahe* (3), *yamāntakāya vi* (0), *agniṣṭhāntebhyo vi* (0). Then, for Kullāmālinī: *nṛḷḹ thaca dhīṇu ūbaka khaga ghaṅa iava bhaya ḍaḍha ṭhajha jara ṭapa chalā sa aḥ haṣakṣama śaaṃtea io au dapha mālinyainamaḥ*. Thus, [one worships] in the Śakti-vase. Now, one should worship the Śiva-vase in the center.
First, [worship] Vyomavyāpin; then Aghora, Aghorīśvarī, the Niṣkala [form], along with the limbs (aṅgas), faces, weapons, and the Bhairava-enclosure:
*Oṃ guṃ namo bahurūpabhairavāya*. *Oṃ hrīṃ māyādevyai vauṣaṭ*.
The limbs: *Guṃ* to the heart, *guṃ* to the head, *guṃ* to the crest-lock (*śikhā*), *guṃ* to the armor (*kavaca*), *guṃ* to the eyes, *guṃ* to the weapon (*astra*).

With *hrām*, one worships the limbs; then the entire circle of mantras; then the offering of molasses and other items as the *naivedya*. Then, having brought the disciple forward, one should cause him to perform worship.
Thereafter, beginning from the northeast corner (*īśānakoṇa*), one should worship the eight petals of the *muṇḍayāga* with "Salutation to the Halo of Light" (*prabhāmaṇḍalāya namaḥ*).

Thus, in the center of the *muṇḍa-yāga*, [one should worship] "Hrīṃ, obeisance to Māyādevī" in the jar; on one's own right, "obeisance to Gaṅgā"; on one's own left, "obeisance to Yamunā"; and "obeisance to the Guru" in the center of the lotus. Then, in the eight jars, there is the worship of the seat (*āsana-pūjā*): "Obeisance to Ananta," to Ādhāraśakti, to Pṛthivī, to Kṣīrārṇava, to Bījāṅkura, to Padmāsana, and to Pretāsana.
Salutation to the Unmanā state, which is the seat of the *praṇava*. In these jars, Bhairava together with his faces is to be worshipped:
*guṃ* to Bahurūpa Bhairava, *vauṣaṭ*, *svadhā*; *oṃ ḷṃ* to Sadyojāta, *svadhā*; *oṃ vaṃ* to Vāmadeva; *oṃ raṃ* to Aghora;
*oṃ yaṃ* to Tatpuruṣa; *oṃ kṣaṃ* to Īśāna; *oṃ haḥ* to the Weapon (*astra*) of infinite power, *phaṭ*; *hauṃ* to the undecaying power (*alupta-śakti*).

HAIṂ to the armor (kavaca) of independent power from the eyes; HŪṂ to the crest-lock (śikhā) of primordial awakening; HĪṂ to the head of satisfaction; HĀṂ to the heart of omniscience; HRĪṂ to the goddess Māyā, svadhā namaḥ—in the center. Then, in the lamps: OṂ HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ AḤ to Mahālakṣmī, svadhā namaḥ.

Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ṅaṃ cāmuṇḍāyai svadhā namaḥ (3) | Ñaṃ vārāhyai (0) (3) | Ṇaṃ aindryai (0) (3) | Naṃ vaiṣṇavyai (0) (3) | Maṃ kaumāryai (0) (3) | Vaṃ māheśvaryai (0) (3) | Haṃ brāhmyai svadhā namaḥ || I bow to the self-luminous one; thus [offering] to the Self as Śiva, [with] incense, lamps, and so forth: today, to the weapon, to the power (śakti), and to the deities of the Śiva-vessel.

To Saṃhārabhairava, Bhīṣaṇabhairava, Kapāleśabhairava, Unmattabhairava, Krodharājabhairava, Caṇḍabhairava, Rurubhairava, Asitāṅgabhairava; to Mahālakṣmī, Cāmuṇḍā, Vārāhī, Aindrī, Vaiṣṇavī, Kaumārī, Māheśvarī, and Brāhmī—homage to the incense! Homage to the lamp! [With the sacred thread] over the right shoulder (apasavya): to the father and mother, of the Bhairava lineage.

[Offer] incense with *svadhā namaḥ* at the Muṇḍayāga; [offer] the lamp with *svadhā namaḥ*. With the left hand: "We know that Great Lord... (3); to those suffering in the southeast... (3); to Yamāntaka... (3). Now, for the weapon (*astra*), the spear (*śakti*), the deities of the Śiva-pitcher (*kalaśa*), Saṃhārabhairava, Mahālakṣmī, and for one's own father and mother.

[In the] Bhairavagotra, for other rites of worship: the weapon-vessel, the power-vessel, the Śiva-vessel; [the eight Bhairavas] beginning with Saṃhāra; [and] the Mahālakṣmīs—(2)—I shall perform the worship, the adoration. Having scattered barley grains, [performing] the seating in this very manner up to the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), then the lamp-worship with the right hand: "Salutations to you, O Great Goddess, [remover of] all calamities..."

In the destroyer, whose nature resides in the form of desire; in Śivā, who is eternal and of the nature of eternity; who is free from the stain of time; who dwells in the midst of existence and non-existence; who is unmanifest and beyond all calculation; who is peaceful, eternal, and without fluctuation; who is supreme and devoid of both dissolution and emergence; who is eternally satisfied and free from ailment; in the seed of power (Śakti-bīja) which abides in its own nature; in Caṇḍakāpālinī, the Sovereign Lady; in the utterance of Svāhā.
O Goddess, you who are perfected in the utterance of *svadhā* and supreme in compassion, you abide as the pervader of all the gods;
this entire creation of beings, moving and unmoving, is pervaded by you. O Lord, for the sake of our fulfillment today, grant us your presence!
[With the offering made] counter-clockwise: *Namaḥ* to the Red One, to the Fierce One, to the One with Fierce Eyes, to the One of Great Sighs, to the Terrifying One, and to the One with Teeth.

To Bhīmavaktrā, the one of great strength, the ender of Yama, [I offer this] today for the sake of increasing the illumination in the next world of my father or mother, [born of the] Bhairava lineage, for the sake of dispelling the darkness of the terrible and the darkness of delusion during the funeral rites, and for the sake of attaining the state of Śiva: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aḥ, the lamp of Mahālakṣmī.
I offer salutations with the right hand; *namostute* with the left hand to Yamāntaka;

*piturbhairava*. *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ṅaṃ*, the lamp of Cāmuṇḍī; *namostute* with the right hand; *namostute* with the left hand to Yamāntaka; *piturbhairava*. *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ñaṃ*, the lamp of Vārāhī; *namostute* with the right hand.

[With the right hand] *namo 'stu te* [with the left hand] *yamāntakāya* [for the father] *bhairava*. *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ṇaṃ aindrī dīpaṃ* [with the right hand] *namo 'stu te* [with the left hand] *yamāntakāḥ* [for the father] *bhairava*. *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ naṃ vaiṣṇavī* [with the right hand] *namo 'stu te* [with the left hand] *yamāntakā* [for the father] *bhairava*. *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ maṃ kaumārī* [with the right hand].

With the right hand: *namo'stu te*. With the left hand (*apasavyena*): to Yamāntaka. To the Father Bhairava: *oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ vaṃ māhīśvarī*. With the right hand: *namo'stu te*. With the left hand: to Yamāntaka. To the Father Bhairava: *oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ haṃ brāhmī dīpaṃ*. Today, for the sake of the Father Bhairava’s funeral rites (*antyeṣṭi*), [I offer] to the Saṃhāra-Bhairava and the others.
"May [the deity] be pleased through the pleasure of the eight goddesses of the Ṣṭakasada. Thus ends the worship of the Muṇḍayāga.

Now, the worship of the Māyājāla: having placed the jewel-lamp and the water-pot in the center, and having stationed the eight Kṣetrapālas outside, one should ask forgiveness from the Dūtī and the musical instruments. One should offer incense with the mantra beginning 'naumi svātma...'"

Having resolved upon the lamp offering, [one should offer] today, starting from now, to Bahurūpabhairava accompanied by Māyādevī, to Āmardaka, Kaṅkāla, Bhīmarāva, Aṭṭahāsa, Karavīra, the one named Karaṅka, Kālagrāsa, and Kuleśvara; and to Heruka in the east: Oṃ hrāṃ kṣaṃ kṣūṃ.
Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ lāṃ kṣīṃ, to Tripurāntaka in the southeast; oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ kṣīṃ, to Vetāla in the south;
oṃ hrīṃ kṣūṃ hūṃ, to Agnijihva in the southwest; oṃ hrīṃ phrīṃ hūṃ, to Kurpara in the west; oṃ kṣāṃ yūṃ kṣīṃ, to Kāla in the northwest; oṃ ū āṃ yūṃ kṣmīṃ, to Ekapāda in the northeast.

*Oṃ kṣāṃ yūṃ kṣīṃ*, [I offer] incense, *svadhā namaḥ*, and light, *svadhā namaḥ*, to Bhīmarūpa in the center, to Ḍāmara above, and to Hāṭakeśvara below. With the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*apasavyena*), [I offer] incense, *svadhā namaḥ*, and light, *svadhā namaḥ*, today to the father Bhairava. [Then follows] the worship of the seat in the central jar with the sacred thread over the left shoulder (*savyena*).

Having prepared the seat with: "Salutation to Āsana-ayana; to the foundational power (Ādhāraśakti); to the Earth; to the Ocean of Milk; to the Sprout of the Seed; to the Lotus Seat; to the Preta Seat; to the Praṇava Seat; salutation to Unmanā.
Then, on the left [of the seat], "Salutation to Gaṅgā"; on the right, "Salutation to Yamunā"; on one's own left, "Salutation to the Guru"; and to the Paramaguru.

Salutation to the supreme preceptor, the supreme Āditya, and to the primordial Siddhas. In the center, salutation to Ananta; [salutation] to Dharma; salutation to the pericarp (*karṇikā*). Upon that, in a vessel filled with substances, one should worship everything beginning with Gaṇeśa for those who have received initiation (*dīkṣita*). One should worship the partless (*niṣkala*) and the multiform (*bahurūpa*); for those who have not received initiation, [one should worship] Bhairava.

Having meditated in his mind upon him—whose meditation is white, who has three eyes, five faces, and ten arms, who holds a spear, a trident, a rosary, a sword, and a boon-granting gesture in his right hands, and who is surrounded by a citron, a bow, a shield, a jar, and a mirror in his left hands; who is encompassed by the ninefold self and who joyfully brings an end to the goddess Māyā—one should worship him. Thus, having meditated with the mind...

Having worshipped the venerable one, one should worship [the deities] in the water-pot (*kalaśa*) upon the seat that has been worshipped: *Oṃ guṃ bahurūpabhairavāya vauṣaṭ svadhā namaḥ |* *Oṃ laṃ sadyojātāya svadhā namaḥ |* *Vaṃ vāmadevāya svadhā namaḥ |* *Raṃ aghorāya svadhā namaḥ |* *Yaṃ tatpuruṣāya svadhā namaḥ |* *Kṣaṃ īśānāya svadhā namaḥ |* *Oṃ haḥ anantaśaktaye astrāya phaṭ |*

Oṃ hāuṃ, obeisance to the eyes of the one whose power is undiminished; Oṃ haiṃ, obeisance to the armor of the independent one; Oṃ hūṃ, obeisance to the crest-lock of primordial awakening; Oṃ hīṃ, obeisance to the head of contentment; Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the heart of omniscience. One should also worship the Goddess. One should always meditate upon the Goddess Māyā, who is seated on the lap of the Supreme Lord, possessed of fresh youth, dark-complexioned, two-armed, and holding a noose and a goad in her hands. Having thus meditated: Oṃ hrīṃ, svadhā and obeisance to the Goddess Māyā, who is seated on the lap of the Supreme Lord. In this manner, having completed the worship...

With the left hand [holding] the bowstring for Maheśa, for those in the south-east for Agniṣṭha, for Yamāntaka in the south, for Apasavya in the west, and for Āmardaka and the others, for Heruka and the others, for Māyādevī, for myself, and for my father Bhairava—
in order to increase the manifestation [of merit] in the other world for him— I perform this worship and offering of the *Māyājāla*. Thus it was.

[The ritual] begins with water for the feet (*nādi*), incense (*gandha*), the water offering (*argha*), and flowers (*puṣpa*), and ends with the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*). With the left hand: "Homage to You" (*namo 'stu te*). With the right hand (in the *apasavya* position): "To Yamāntaka" (*yamāntakāya*).
Today, for my father Bhairava, I offer the lamp of Māyādevī.
For the initiated [disciple], I offer the lamp of Aghorīśvarī. Today, for my father Bhairava, Māyādevī...

May the Kṣetrapālas of Āmardaka together with their retinues be pleased; may they be gratified. Having worshipped the deity to be meditated upon by those who have received initiation, one should mutter the root mantra one hundred and eight times. Having prostrated, one should perform the proclamation of the name, saying: "May [Name], who consists of the letters of the Mātṛkās of the Muṇḍayāga, be victorious. Thus ends the *Māyājāla-pūjā*.
[He should perform] the fire-ritual (*agni-sādhana*). Then, having prepared the vessel for the *arghya* offering for the weapon (*astra*) according to his own skill, [he should recite]:
Oṃ ślīpaśu hūṃ phaṭ, to the Pāśupata weapon, phaṭ! Oṃ hṛdayāya phaṭ namaḥ (to the heart, phaṭ, obeisance)! Oṃ ślīṃ śirase phaṭ svāhā (to the head, phaṭ, svāhā)!
Śrīṃ śikhāyai phaṭ vaṣaṭ (to the crest-lock, phaṭ, vaṣaṭ)! Śrīṃ kavacāya phaṭ hūṃ (to the armor, phaṭ, hūṃ)! Hūṃ netrebhyaḥ phaṭ vauṣaṭ (to the eyes, phaṭ, vauṣaṭ)!

*Phaṭ astrāya phaṭ phaṭ*. "Salutation to the Sword of Knowledge (*jñānakhaḍga*), which consists of the thirty-six principles (*ṣaṭtriṃśattattva*). Having thus worshipped it with perfumes, water for honor (*arghya*), and flowers, one should perform the purification of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa-saṃskāra*) with the Sword of Knowledge using the water from the vessel of the weapon-offering (*astrārghyapātra*), as follows: *Oṃ phaṭ, I perform the sprinkling, phaṭ. Oṃ phaṭ, I perform the scraping, phaṭ.*

Oṃ phaṭ, I perform the cleansing, phaṭ! Oṃ phaṭ, I perform the extraction of the clay, phaṭ! Oṃ phaṭ, I perform the kneading, phaṭ! Oṃ phaṭ, I perform the drying, phaṭ! Oṃ phaṭ, I perform the sprinkling, phaṭ!

Oṃ Ḷṃ, obeisance to the fire-pit (kuṇḍa), whose essence is the power of action (kriyā-śakti); obeisance to Dhātrī; obeisance to Brahmā; obeisance to Kālāgnirudra. Thus ends the worship of the fire-pit. Oṃ Hsrrīṃ Daka (2) Kaha (2) Jvala (2) Sarvadhāma Mahādhāma Sarvaga Sarveśvara Sarvabhakṣaka Sarvamantrārciṣe Jaya (2) Bhairavāgnaye Kālāgnaye.
*Śuddhatejase hūṃ phaṭ* (3) *svāhā*. These are the seventy-three syllables. *Haḥ phaṭ*, "I perform the vajrī-karaṇa," *phaṭ*;

with this, one performs the vajrī-karaṇa in the center of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*). Then, having placed one blade of *darbha* grass with its tip pointing east and another with its tip pointing north in the center of the pit, one should worship the seat at the crossroads with: *Oṃ vāgīśyāsanāya namaḥ*. Thus one worships the pedestal.

One should recite: *oṃ phaṭ agner avaguṇṭhanaṃ karomi phaṭ*—this is the veiling (*avaguṇṭhana*). Then, worship with: *raṃ jñānaśaktyātmane agnaye namaḥ*. Then, with the mantra *oṃ phaṭ kravyādaṃ niṣkarṣayāmi phaṭ*, [one should perform the expulsion] using *darbha* grass.
Having ignited two fuel-sticks (*kāṇḍa*), one should cast them into the south-western direction. Then, there are the oblations of sesame seeds: *oṃ raṃ agneḥ kravyāda-śuddhiṃ karomi svāhā*.
[Fifth oblation: *oṃ hūṃ agneḥ darbhattrayeṇācchādanaṃ karomi hūṃ*.
Having covered the fire with three blades of *darbha* grass, one should then take the vessel of fire with both hands and [touch it] with the tip of the nose.

Having first smelled [the substance] with the state of consciousness, having grasped the tip of the flame with the root-mantra, and having caused it to enter the heart through the left nostril by means of inhalation (*pūraka*), one unifies it with the fire of one's own consciousness; then, exhaling (*recaka*) through the right nostril while uttering the root-mantra, one should cast it into the vessel of fire. "Namaḥ to the Self, namaḥ to Agni; hāṃ [to the limbs]. With that very [mantra], perform the rite of immortalization (*amṛtīkaraṇa*). Firmly grasping the identification with Śiva, thinking "I myself am indeed Śiva," meditate on the Fire in the form of semen and conceive Māyā as Vāgīśī.

The concealment of the entrance: *Oṃ hūṃ vāhaḥ phaṭ*, "I fashion the enclosure for the dice, *namaḥ*. Oṃ raṃ! I perform the *puṃsavana* (the rite for ensuring a male child) for Agni; svāhā! (3) Oṃ raṃ! May the *puṃsavana* for Agni be accomplished; svāhā! (3) Oṃ raṃ! I perform the *sīmantonnayana* (the parting of the hair) for Agni; svāhā! (3) May it be thus accomplished; svāhā! (3) Oṃ raṃ!
Homage to Agni becoming one whose limbs are differentiated—having thus drawn across the entire body of Agni with the tip of a blade of *kuśa* grass.

Oṃ raṃ, salutation to the one whose form is fire—thus is the worship. Oṃ juṃ, svāhā! I perform the visualization of the eastern face of Agni. Oṃ hūṃ, svāhā! (3) May it be thus accomplished. (3) Now, the meditation: One should contemplate the Fire-god as red, wearing matted locks and red garments, seated upon the lap of Svāhā, two-armed, with red eyes, [mounted] on the back of a parrot.

May Sadāśiva forgive [me]; one should release the northern seat. To Viṣṇu in the west, "namaḥ"; "Gandhādi-puṣpaṃ viṣṇave svāhā" (3). May Viṣṇu forgive [me]...

One should release the previous seat (*viṣṭara*). *Oṃ hāṃ vāgīśvaryai namaḥ*—[offer] perfumes and so forth. *Oṃ hāṃ vāgīśvaryai namaḥ svāhā*. [Perform] the libation (*tarpaṇa*): "O Goddess Vāgīśvarī, who bestows creation, maintenance, dissolution, enjoyment, and liberation, salutations to you; go to your own celestial realm. Having thus dismissed her, [one should proceed] again to the Bhairava-fire.

For the purpose of warding off saliva during twenty-four oblations of breath-blowing measured by the span of the hand: *oṃ juṃ saḥ bhairavāgniṃ tarpayāmi svāhā* (24). Now, the consecration of the *sruk* and *sruva* ladles: *haḥ phaṭ*, I perform the heating;
*phaṭ*.

"HAḤ PHAṬ, I perform the heating in the fire, PHAṬ"—thus [is performed] the sprinkling with auspicious water (*śivāmbhas*). "OṂ HUṂ, I veil, HUṂ"—thus [is performed] the veiling. In this manner, there is contact with the front by means of the front. Again, the heating and sprinkling of the *brāhmaṇa* [blade] in the fire; contact with the middle by means of the middle of the *darbha* grass. Again, the heating and sprinkling of the *brāhmaṇa* [blade] with the root mantra (*mūla*).

Furthermore, regarding the initial contact (*mūlasparśa*): one should sprinkle the Brahmin with water while reciting the *tāpana* mantra. Then, having placed [the two blades] face-down upon the back of the sword of knowledge (*jñānakhaḍga*), one should worship them as the forms of Śiva and Śakti. Having worshipped them with "Obeisance to Śiva and Śakti" (*śivaśaktibhyāṃ namaḥ*), one should turn them face-up and offer scents, water for honor (*argha*), flowers, and so forth, saying "Oṃ Ātma... [to Śiva] and "Obeisance to Śiva" (*śivāya namaḥ*) and "Obeisance to Śakti" (*śaktaye namaḥ*).
"Tvā-ya-namaḥ" at the base; "Juṃ vidyā-tattvāya namaḥ" in the middle; "Saḥ śiva-tattvāya namaḥ" on the head.
This is the consecration (*saṃskāra*) of the *sruk* and *sruva* ladles. Now, the consecration of the clarified butter (*ājya*). Placing the clarified butter on the fire;
placing the vessel containing the flowing butter after it has been sprinkled with water; "Phaṭ, I perform the heating, Phaṭ"; "Oṃ huṃ, I veil [it]."

*Mihuṃ* is the veiling. *Oṃ phaṭ, I perform the sprinkling, phaṭ*: thus, the sprinkling with water from the weapon-mantra (*astra*). *Phaṭ, I perform the heating, phaṭ*: again, the heating for the sake of illumination. *Oṃ hūṃ, I perform the dismissal, hūṃ*: [the maintenance] in the direction of Agni. *Dī*... [maintenance].
For the sake of making the meaning clear: one performs three circumambulations around the *kuṇḍa* with the mantra "Oṃ phaṭ, I perform the circumambulation, phaṭ.

Then follows the installation of the *yoni*. Next, taking two stalks of *darbha* grass, each a span (*prādeśa*) in length and shaped like a serpent’s noose (*nāgapāśa*), with both hands using the thumbs and ring fingers, one performs the threefold drawing away of the clarified butter (*ājya*) from the fire, which is the act of leaping over (*utplavana*) and merging together (*saṃplava*).

One should prepare a forest [of grass] for the purpose of preserving the essential portion and removing the non-essential portion by means of the root mantra: *oṃ juṃ saḥ utplavanam karomi phaṭ* and *oṃ juṃ saḥ saṃplavanam karomi phaṭ*. Thereafter, having ignited a darbha torch, one should cast it into the middle of the vessel of clarified butter (*ājyapātra*) by means of the root mantra. Furthermore, with that blazing darbha torch, [one should circle it] on all sides.
Having performed the *nīrājana* with "Bhrāmyate na phaṭ nīrājanam karomi phaṭ," one should cast [the offering] into the fire.

Having consecrated it with the root mantra along with its limbs (*sāṅga*) and rendered it nectarine (*amṛtīkṛtya*) by means of the *Amṛteśa-mudrā*, [one should place it] upon the vessel of clarified butter (*ājya-pātra*).

Having placed two stalks of *darbha* grass facing east with the root-mantra (*mūla*), one should worship the three channels (*nāḍī*) in three parts as follows: in the center, "Salutation to Suṣumṇā"; on the right, "Salutation to Piṅgalā"; on the left, "Salutation to Iḍā. Then, for the fire: "Oṃ, salutation; I perform the division of the fire of Bhairava into three parts. [Then] for that which rests in Iḍā...

*Māyā* (the Illusion), obeisance to the Sun residing in the *piṅgalā* on the right; obeisance to Agni residing in the *suṣumṇā* on the left; [obeisance] to the middle. Then, from the southern portion of the [western] part, in the southeastern quarter: *Oṃ juṃ saḥ agnaye svāhā* (1). From the northern portion of the [eastern] part, in the northeastern quarter: *Oṃ juṃ saḥ somāya svāhā* (2).
From the middle portion of the clarified butter, into the middle portion of the fire: *oṃ juṃ saḥ agnīṣomābhyāṃ svāhā* (3).

Thus for the bright fortnight; now for the dark fortnight, "Sūrya" is substituted in place of "Soma," and [the offering is made] from the left portion of the clarified butter into the left portion of the fire.
Oṃ juṃ saḥ agnaye svāhā (1). From the southern portion of the clarified butter (*ājya*), [offer] into the southern portion of the fire. Oṃ juṃ saḥ sūryāya svāhā (2).

From the middle portion of the clarified butter, [offer] into the middle portion of the fire. Oṃ juṃ saḥ agnisūryābhyāṃ svāhā (3). Thus for the dark fortnight (*kṛṣṇapakṣa*). Now follows the *cākṣuṣahoma*: with clarified butter, [recite] "Oṃ juṃ saḥ, I perform the consumption [of the offering] for Bhairava-Agni, svāhā" (3).

Oṃ juṃ saḥ, let the consumption by the fire of Bhairava be accomplished, svāhā! (3) Likewise: to Agni, svāhā; to Sūrya, svāhā; to Agni and Sūrya, svāhā; to the vessel of oblation, svāhā; to the clarified butter (ājya), namaḥ klīṃ; to the sesame seeds, namaḥ haṃ; to the rice grains, namaḥ saṃ; Oṃ hūṃ hāṃ hīṃ hūṃ haiṃ hauṃ haḥ hūṃ, I perform the *sampāta* offering, svāhā—thus [he offers] into the fire with "hā."
In this manner, the oblation is poured into the *vati*. Then follows the inspection of the clarified butter (*ājya*): "Clarified butter is declared to be splendor;
clarified butter is the supreme remover of sin. Clarified butter is the food of the gods; upon clarified butter the worlds are established."

May whatever sin has been incurred through divine, atmospheric, terrestrial, and other such [causes], all of that reach total destruction upon contact with the clarified butter (ājya). O father, belonging to the Bhairava lineage, may you proceed toward the supreme state of Śiva and attain the state of liberation in the fire of Bhairava.
