To the one adorned with jewels in the midst of a thousand rays; to the one possessing a thousand enjoyments; to the one with two thousand eyes; to the one with two thousand tongues; to the one surrounded by ten million nāgas; to the one clad in yellow garments; to the one who holds a mace in his hand; to the infinite nāga-king; upon whose back [sits] the one seated upon a lotus: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ rāṃ rājñī.

*Oṃ namo bhagavatyai svāhā* (108). *Śītāṃśubālārka*. *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ rāṃ klīṃ sauḥ bhagavatyai rām*—thus the limbs (*aṅga*). *Oṃ hrīṃ vijayāyai svā*, *hrāṃ jaganmātre*, *hrauṃ jayāyai*, *hraḥ jagaddhātryai svā*. Now, the Jvālā [mantra]: *Jvālāparvata*. O you whose long locks of hair are bound with the flames of the fire at the end of the aeon (*kalpānta*).

O Mother, O cruel-faced one, O daughter of Vaikartana, you of firm vows! *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ huṃ jvālā bhagavatyai namaḥ svāhā* (108). To Lakṣmī, svāhā; to Ṛddhi, svāhā; to Tuṣṭi, svāhā; to Puṣṭi, svāhā; to Svadhā, svāhā; to Svāhā, svāhā; to Dhṛti, svāhā; to Martyā, svāhā; to Jvālāmukhī, svāhā. O Jvālāmukhī of great power! *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ jvālāmukhi, devour all my enemies!* (2).

HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ (108). I worship Kāmeśvara, who possesses the luster of ten million moons, who bears the moon upon his crest, who has three eyes, and whose hands hold the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, as well as a trident and a sword. OṂ HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ AṂ KĀMEŚVARABHAIRAVĀYA NAMAḤ SVĀHĀ (108).
He has three eyes, a crown of jewels with the half-moon, OṂ HRĀṂ HVAUṂ MAHĀDEVĀYA NAMAḤ SVĀHĀ (108). HRĀM is the limb.

Meditation: *Oṃ hrāṃ vāṃ vāmadevāya namaḥ svāhā* (108 times). *Hrāṃ* for the limbs. I meditate in my mind upon Bhūteśvara, who shines like a jasmine flower or the moon, who has the crescent moon as his crest-jewel, who holds a skull, a noose, a goad, and a trident in his hands, who is three-eyed, white with sacred ash, and laughing. *Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ bhūteśvarāya namaḥ svāhā* (108 times). [He is] like the rising moon...

I worship Bhavānī, who has four faces and four arms, whose lotus-eyes are red, who smiles radiantly, who is marked by the sword, the spear, the gesture of granting boons (*varada*), and the gesture of fearlessness (*abhaya*), and who stands upon a corpse; she whom I honor in my heart. *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ bhuvaneśvaryai namaḥ svāhā* (108 times).
*Hrāṃ* for the limbs. *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ chrāṃ grāṃ mahāmāyāyai namaḥ svāhā* (108 times). [The skull of the universe...]

I meditate upon Bhadrakālī, who resembles a fresh rain cloud and sits amidst the dead; she holds the hand of her creator upon the palm of her lotus-hand, laughing, never satiated, and constantly devouring all people; and she, dark-hued, forcibly holds Viṣṇu and Śiva by their arms, with the trident piercing them.
KRĪM KRĪM KRĪM HŪM HŪM HRĪM HRĪM BHAIM BHADRAKĀLI BHAIM HRĪM HRĪM HŪM HŪM KRĪM KRĪM KRĪM SVĀHĀ (108). This is the six-limbed mantra (*ṣaḍaṅga*).

Mahārudra, who dwells in the cremation ground, is naked, possessing a skull-cup and a flaying-knife in his left hands, and a trident and a khaṭvāṅga staff in his right. Though his limbs are adorned with serpents, he is further embellished with ashes, bones, and jewels. Standing amidst a blazing fire, he rests upon a bed of ashes. There, in the reverse posture of sexual union, he drinks the blood from the heart of Kālikā.
Having made both the solid food (dyañca) and the soft food (coṣya) mutually [exchanged], one should thus worship the God with devotion; all perfections (siddhis) are thereby produced.

HŪṂ HŪṂ MAHĀKĀLA PRASĪDA HRĪṂ HRĪṂ SVĀHĀ (108). Now, one should perform the purification of hell for those who have not been initiated, as follows: "These terrible hells are proclaimed to be triangular, intended for the casting down of living beings devoted to evil deeds. OṂ HŪṂ HĀṂ, [for] so-and-so, in the element of earth within the *nivṛtti-kalā*, [the spirits] Kuṣmāṇḍas..."

...antaḥavīcinarakaṃ śodhayāmi svāhā (3). (1) Oṃ hūṃ hāṃ, of such-and-such a person, in the element of earth within the kalā of nivṛtti, I purify the inner raurava hell up to the kūṣmāṇḍas; svāhā (3). (2) Oṃ hūṃ hāṃ, of such-and-such a person, I purify the kumbhīpāka hell... (3). (3) Oṃ [hūṃ hāṃ], of such-and-such a person, I purify the tāmisra hell... (3). (4) Oṃ [hūṃ hāṃ], of such-and-such a person, [I purify] the andhatāmisra...
[Name], a portion of the Sañjīvana hell; [Name], a portion of the Kālasūtra hell;
[Name], a portion of the Sūci hell.
[Name], from the Mahākāya hell; [Name], from the Kṣuradhāra hell; [Name], from the Asipatra hell; [Name], from the Asitāla hell;
[Name], from the Drūsamasta hell; [Name], from the Tīkṣṇaṇḍa hell; [Name].

Oṃ amuka, I purify the portion of the Vajratuṇḍa hell, svāhā! Oṃ amuka, I purify the portion of the Ambharīṣa hell, svāhā! Oṃ amuka, I purify the portion of the Aṅgarāśi hell, svāhā! Oṃ amuka, I purify the portion of the Asṛkpūra hell, svāhā! Then the full oblation: Oṃ hūṃ hāṃ, may there be the purification of the fifty million hells, svāhā phaṭ! Then the command: Nara...

"O center, by the command of such-and-such Śiva, you have been bound; you must not act [otherwise]. May he go to the state free from suffering. One should not perform this for one who has already been initiated (*dīkṣita*). *oṃ brāhmyai śabdam arpayāmi svāhā* (3) *oṃ māheśvaryai sparśam arpayāmi svāhā* (3) *oṃ vaiṣṇavyai rūpam arpayāmi svāhā* (3) *oṃ vārāhyai gandham arpayāmi...*

I offer intellect to Yāmī, svāhā! (3) Oṃ, I offer intellect to Aindrī, svāhā! (3) Oṃ, I offer ego-sense to Cāmuṇḍā, svāhā! (3) Oṃ, I offer mind to Mahālakṣmī, svāhā! (3). Now follows the consecration of the corpse (śava-saṃskāra).

Then, near the fire, having seated the *śava* (the corpse) upon a seat of *darbha* grass consecrated with the weapon-mantra (*astramantra*) facing north, one should strike its head with the sword of knowledge (*jñānakhaḍga*), with ashes, and with the weapon-mantra. Having sprinkled [it] from the vessel of the weapon-offering (*astrārghya-pātra*) with the mantra: *oṃ hāṃ hīṃ hūṃ haiṃ hauṃ haḥ*, one should perform the deposition of the principles (*tattvanyāsa*) upon its body with flowers, starting from the feet and ending at the head, [measuring] a finger-breadth.

One should perform the initiation from the feet up to the heart. Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) using the formula: *Oṃ aṃ hrīṃ saḥ pṛthivyai svadhā namaḥ*, at a distance of four finger-breadths above the ankles; likewise: *Oṃ aṃ hrīṃ saḥ jalāya svadhā namaḥ*; *Oṃ tejasai svadhā namaḥ*; *Oṃ vāyave svadhā namaḥ*; *Oṃ ākāśāya svadhā namaḥ*; *Oṃ gandhāya svadhā namaḥ*; *Oṃ rasāya svadhā namaḥ*; *Oṃ sparśāya svadhā namaḥ*.

(4) Svā for speech; (4) svā for the organ of generation; (4) svā for the anus; (4) svā for the feet; (4) svā for the hands; (4) svā for speech; (4) svā for the nose; (4) svā for the tongue; (4) svā for the eye; (4) svā for the skin; (4) svā for the ear; (4) svā for the mind; (4) svā for the ego-sense; (4) svā for the intellect; (4) svā for primordial nature. Thus, twenty-four [syllables].

One should worship you. Then one should recite the *dhāraṇā*. First, having performed the excellence of the exhalation (*recaka*), inhalation (*pūraka*), and retention (*kumbhaka*) of one's own vital breaths, and having experienced rest in the state of Śiva at the "twelve-finger limit" (*dvādaśānta*) preceded by the utterance of the *praṇava*, one pervades the entire body—which consists of all things—with a mind that is beyond the mental faculty (*aunmanasika*), [filling] the column of the *suṣumṇā*.
Having gone to the support of the unborn [state] by way of the path, then— according to the principle beginning with "this entire sixfold path,
though very extensive, is established in a single prāṇa"—
one should awaken the *prāṇakuṇḍalinī*, which consists of the entire path, through the channel of the *suṣumṇā* stalk as far as the *dvādaśānta*, along with all the channels.

Having performed the transformation into Bhairava by filling [the breath] with *stha*, one should project that [power], which has the form of a column of smoke, pervading as far as the *manas* through the path of the nostril— according to the principle that "there is no other supreme Vidyā-Mātṛkā"— in the form of a web of mantras (*vidyajāla*). Thereby, from the midst of the path of phonemes (*varṇādhvan*) within the womb of non-duality, one should [extract] the form of the first letter of the name of the person to be accomplished (*sādhya*).

Having withdrawn the living soul, which has the form of a star and is the size of a thumb, by means of the *saṃhāramudrā*, [the practitioner] causes it to enter his own heart through the path of the left nostril; having led it to the seat of birth (*janmādhāra*), he encloses it within the *praṇava* (Oṃ) of his own vital breath, and having exited through the right nostril, he causes it to enter the heart of the corpse through its left passage with the mantra: *oṃ hūṃ devadattātmane hūṃ*.

Oṃ hūṃ, salutation to the Puruṣatattva. (25) Then, arising from the *mūlādhāra* in a subtle form and pervading the staff-like path of the infinite channels (*nāḍī*), it ascends by its power; reaching the space of the nose, it emits a mass of extremely radiant flames as beautiful as smoke, which, being cast forth, covers the wheel of the paths until the desired goal is attained.

This is the ritual application named the Great Net for bringing forth the living soul (*jīvānayana*). Having thus drawn forth the living soul, one should install the *puruṣatattva*. Then, the worship of the corpse with flowers should be performed. By this method, one should install the *puruṣatattva* at a distance of three finger-breadths [from the heart]. OṂ HAṂ DEVADATTĀTMANE OṂ HŪṂ PURUṢATATTVĀYA NAMAḤ. (25) Thus.

To Kāla (36): *Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ namaḥ* to the principle (*tattva*) of Time (4); *ṃ* to the principle of Necessity (0) (4); *ṃ* to the principle of Attachment (0) (4); *ṃ* to the principle of Knowledge (0) (4); *ṃ* to the principle of Time (0) (4); *ṃ* to the principle of Illusion (*māyā*) (0). Thus, the six principles ending with *kalā* [are worshipped] individually with flowers and other offerings at three finger-breadths (*aṅgula*) each. This makes eighteen finger-breadths. To Māyā (31).
Oṃ Hrīṃ, salutations to the principle of Pure Knowledge (Śuddhavidyā-tattva) (4); salutations to the principle of Īśvara (4); salutations to the principle of Sadāśiva (4).
The four principles beginning with Māyā and ending with Sadāśiva each occupy four finger-breadths;
thus, they total sixteen finger-breadths. In this manner, together with the previous [principles], [the space] from the feet up to the forehead is the supreme [region].
By this [measurement], there are eighty-four finger-breadths (*aṅgula*) from the *parāpara* up to the *brahmarandhra*;

ninety-six finger-breadths from the *paramāṇu* up to the *dvādaśānta*; and one hundred and eight finger-breadths in total. Then, with "Obeisance to Śakti" (35) and "Obeisance to Śiva" (36), [one should worship] as the all-pervading reality of Śiva and Śakti.

One should perform the placement [of the letters] in this manner. Then, according to the method stated in the *Tantrāloka*, after the internal placement of the principles (*tattva-nyāsa*), the placement of the *Mātṛkā* of the Purifier (*śodhaka-mālinī-mātṛkā*) should be performed upon that, following the sequence of the fingers.
As follows: thereafter, the placement of the *Mātṛkā* on the corpse is performed from the feet up to the head.
Oṃ kṣaṃ, salutation to Mātṛkā; oṃ phaṃ, salutation to Mālinī; oṃ haṃ, salutation to Mātṛkā;
daṃ, salutation to Mālinī; saṃ, salutation to Mātṛkā; auṃ, salutation to Mālinī; ṣaṃ, salutation to Mātṛkā; oṃ, salutation to Mālinī;
śaṃ, salutation to Mātṛkā; aiṃ, salutation to Mālinī; vaṃ, salutation to Mātṛkā; eṃ, salutation to Mālinī; laṃ, salutation to Mātṛkā.
To Taṃ Mālinī (0), Raṃ Mātṛkā (0), Aṃ Mālinī (0), Yaṃ Mātṛkā (0), Śaṃ Mālinī (na),
Maṃ Mātṛkā (0), Maṃ Mālinī (0), Bhaṃ Mātṛkā (0), Kṣaṃ Mālinī (0), Baṃ Mātṛkā (na), Ṣaṃ Mālinī (0), Phaṃ Mātṛkā (0), Haṃ Mālinī (0), Paṃ Mātṛkā (0), Aḥ Mālinī (0).
To Naṃ Mātṛkā (0), to Saṃ Mālinī (0); to Dhaṃ Mātṛkā (0), to Āṃ Mālinī (0); to Daṃ Mātṛkā (na), to Laṃ Mālinī (0); to Vaṃ Mātṛkā (0), to Chaṃ Mālinī (0); to Uṃ Mātṛkā (0), to Paṃ Mālinī (na);
to Ṇaṃ Mātṛkā (0), to Ṭaṃ Mālinī (0); to Ḍhaṃ Mātṛkā (0), to Raṃ Mālinī (0); to Ḍaṃ Mātṛkā (na).

Obeisance to Jaṃ Mālinī, Ṭhaṃ Mātṛkā, Ñaṃ Mālinī, Ṭaṃ Mātṛkā, Jhaṃ Mālinī, Ñaṃ Mātṛkā, Ṭhaṃ Mālinī, Jhaṃ Mātṛkā, Ḍhaṃ Mālinī, Jaṃ Mātṛkā, Ḍaṃ Mālinī, Chaṃ Mātṛkā, Yaṃ Mālinī, Caṃ Mātṛkā, and Bhaṃ Mālinī.
To Ṭaṃ Mātṛkā (0), Vaṃ Mālinī (0); to Ghaṃ Mātṛkā (0), Aṃ Mālinī (0); to Gaṃ Mātṛkā (naḥ 0), Iṃ Mālinī (0); to Khaṃ Mātṛkā (0), Ṅaṃ Mālinī (0); to Kaṃ Mātṛkā (0), Ghaṃ Mālinī (naḥ 0);
to Aḥ Mātṛkā (0), Gaṃ Mālinī (0); to Aṃ Mātṛkā (0), Khaṃ Mālinī (0); to Auṃ Mātṛkā (yai 0).

Kaṃ to Mālinī, Oṃ to Mātṛkā, Vaṃ to Mālinī, Aiṃ to Mātṛkā, Ūṃ to Mālinī, Namaḥ; Jhaṃ to Mātṛkā, Uṃ to Mālinī, Ḷṃ to Mātṛkā, Ṇaṃ to Mālinī, Ḷṃ to Mātṛkā, Raṃ to Mālinī, Eṃ to Mātṛkā, Dhaṃ to Mālinī, Ṛ to Mātṛkā, Caṃ to Mālinī, Namaḥ.

*Ūṃ* to Mātṛkā, *thaṃ* to Mālinī, *uṃ* to Mātṛkā, *ḷṃ* to Mālinī, *īṃ* to Mātṛkā, *ḷṃ* to Mālinī, *āṃ* to Mātṛkā, *ṛṃ* to Mālinī, *aṃ* to Mātṛkā, and *naṃ* to Mālinī—salutation (*namaḥ*). Having thus performed the *nyāsa* of Mātṛkā and Mālinī: *Oṃ hrīṃ* to Hiraṇyā, *svāhā*; *oṃ jrīṃ* to Kṛṣṇā, *svāhā*.

Oṃ krīṃ kanakāyai svāhā | Oṃ jhrīṃ atiraktāyai svāhā | Oṃ phraiṃ suprabhāyai svāhā | Oṃ khrīṃ raktāyai svāhā | Oṃ bahurūpāyai svāhā || Now follows the Mātṛkā-homa: This thousand-fold homa cuts away all sins; may it lead to the successful completion of the funeral rites for [Name].

*Taḥ* || *Phaṭ guṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ amukasya pāpāni dahāmi phaṭ* (108). The *Navātman* mantra, ending with *phaṭ*, followed by the five *phaṭ*s, then *amukasya*, *pāpāni*, *dahāmi*, and eight *phaṭ*s— this is the thousand-fold *homa* that must be performed.
Then, having filled the vessel with *lataṇḍala* seeds, the Guru should perform the initiation. Next is the *kaulinī-nyāsa* upon the corpse:
*hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ pheṃ aṃ āṃ devi subhage amukasyātmane itarādhvavyāptanivṛttyantargatadharātattvaśodhini hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ pheṃ kaulini svāhā*. [This is performed] from the feet up to the ankles.

*Hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ pheṃ iṃ īṃ Īśvariya, for the self of [name], the purifier of the water-principle (*aptattva*) included within the *Pratiṣṭhā* [kalā] pervading the other paths; *hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ pheṃ Kaulini svāhā*. Thus ends the section on the flames. (2) *Hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ pheṃ uṃ ūṃ Devī Ūrdhvakeśini, for the self of [name], the light included within the *Vidyā* [kalā] pervading the other paths.*

*Stattvaśodhinī* hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ pheṃ kaulini svāhā. Thus, ending at the *nāḍi*. (3) *Hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ pheṃ ṛṃ ṭaṃ devi vikarālike*, [purify] the air element (*vāyatattva*) situated within the *śānti* [kalā] of the self of [Name], *hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ pheṃ kaulini svāhā*. Thus, ending at the *brahmarandhra*. (4) *Hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ pheṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ*...

"O Goddess, O Auspicious One, for the self of [Name], the purifier of the element of space situated within the Śāntyatītā [kalā], HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ KLĪṂ PHEṂ KAULINĪ SVĀHĀ—this is the all-pervading [mantra]. (5) For women, a long vowel should be substituted in place of the short one."
Then, one should offer a hundred oblations for each of all the deities beginning with Gaṇapati, using sesame seeds and tuṇḍala grains.
One should perform the purification of the elements (*tattva-śodhana*) for those who have not been initiated as follows. Then, there is the oblation (*homa*) with clarified butter (*ājya*): "Oṃ!
O Blessed One, having invoked and worshipped the Earth-element (*pṛthvī-tattva*), I offer this oblation. O Blessed One, Earth-element, come (2); be established (2); be present (2);
be well-present (2); be firmly established (2). O Blessed One, Earth-element, accept this water for the feet (*pādya*); obeisance!"
*Arghya*: "Accept the *arghya*, *svadhā*. To those who eat, accept the unbroken rice and flowers, *namas*.
Accept the worship accompanied by the five offerings, *hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. *Āhuti*: "To the earth element, *svāhā* (108).
To Brahmā, the lord of the earth element, *svāhā* (108). *Pūrṇā*: "The earth element of the six paths of [the disciple] named so-and-so..."

*Śuddhos tu svāhā vauṣaṭ!* May Brahmā be forgiven. O Blessed One, having invoked the *aptatva* as before: *Āpastattvāya svāhā* (108); *Āpastattvādhipataye Viṣṇave svāhā* (108). The full oblation: *Oṃ hūṃ amukāṇu saṣaḍadhvāptatva-śuddhos tu svāhā vauṣaṭ*! May Viṣṇu be forgiven. [The *tejastattva*...]

Having invoked and fully worshipped the external [deity], and having offered oblations: *tejastattvāya svāhā* (108); *tejastattvādhipataye rudrāya svāhā* (108). The full oblation: *oṃ hūṃ [Name] āṇu ṣaḍadhva tejastattvaśuddho bhavatu svāhā vauṣaṭ* (3). O Rudra, may you forgive me. Having invoked and fully worshipped the element of air (*vāyustattva*), and having offered oblations: *vāyustattvāya svāhā* (108).

To Īśvara, the presiding deity of the element of air, svāhā! (108) [The full oblation: Oṃ hūṃ yaṃ, may such-and-such person’s purification of the six paths within the element of air be accomplished, svāhā vauṣaṭ! (4) May Īśvara forgive [me]. Having invoked and worshipped the element of space and offered oblations: svāhā to the element of space! (108) To Sadāśiva, the presiding deity of the element of space...
*Yasvāhā* (108).
*Pūrṇā oṃ hūṃ kṣāṃ amukāṇu ṣaḍadhvākāśatattvaśuddhos tu svāhā vauṣaṭ* (5).
May Śiva always forgive [me]. *Ātmatattvāya svāhā* (10) [with sound]; *Vidyātattvāya svāhā* (10) [in a whisper].

*Śivatattvāya svāhā* (10) with the mind. Then one should offer oblations to the thirty-six principles (*tattvas*): *Oṃ pṛthvītattvāya svāhā* (10), *aptattvāya* (10), *tejastattvāya* (10), *vāyutattvāya* (10), *ākāśatattvāya* (10), *gandhatattvāya* (10), *rasatattvāya* (10), *rūpatattvāya* (10), *sparśatattvāya* (10), *śabdatattvāya* (10).
To you (10), to the one who attends (10), to the drinker (10), to the foot (10), to the hand (10), to speech (10),

to the vital breaths (10), to the tongue (10), to the eye (10), to the skin (10), to the ear (10), to the mind (10), to the ego-sense (10), to the intellect (10), to primordial nature (10), to time (10), to necessity (10), to passion (10), to the principle of knowledge (10), to Ka (10).
Lata (10), Māyātattva (10), Śuddhavidyātattva (10), Īśvaratattva (10), Sadāśivatattva (10), Śaktitattva (0) (10), Śivatattva (10), and Śiva-Śakti (10). (36)

Now, the worship of the funeral pyre and the site: "May you be united with all [beings]... [offering] to the Aśvins for the gift of life. With the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*apasavya*), [reciting] "Obeisance to Gāyatrī" (3), "To that Maheśa" (3), and so forth, beginning with "Today, for Īśāna joined with Gaganayuta, for Īśāna," and so on, for the eighteen *Kṣetrapālas*, for the father’s funeral rites (*antyeṣṭikarma*), and for the worship of the funeral pyre and the site, I shall perform the worship.

In this manner, proceeding as far as the southern limit, one should offer the bali to the Lord of the Field (Kṣetrapāla); then, in the Vedic fire, one should offer the oblation beginning with the food offering (naivedya) and the portion for Iḍā, continuing until the final full oblation (pūrṇāhuti); and then the bali to the Mothers of Space (Ākāśamātṛs).

One should recite: "Obeisance to the flesh-eating bulls" (*namaḥ kravyādamukṣebhyaḥ*) for whoever dwells in this field. Then, having returned to the vicinity of the fire with the left hand, one should perform the *homa* sacrifice, offering: "Svāhā to Brahmā," "Svāhā to Viṣṇu," "Svāhā to Rudra," "Svāhā to Īśvara," "Svāhā to Sadāśiva," "Svāhā to the Great Elements" (*mahābhūtebhyaḥ*), and "Svāhā to Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt" (*indrāya vajrahastāya*).
To Yama, who holds a staff in his hand—Svāhā! To Varuṇa, who holds a noose in his hand—Svāhā! To Soma—[Svāhā!

One should offer the *puryaṣṭaka* (the eightfold subtle body) into Brahmā and the others: Oṃ hāṃ, to Brahmā, I offer sound and touch belonging to [Name]—Svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to Viṣṇu, I offer taste belonging to [Name]—Svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, to Rudra...

Having offered separately as follows: "Oṃ hāṃ, I offer the *kaugandharūpa* belonging to [Name], svāhā" (10); "Oṃ hāṃ, to Īśvara, I offer the *kaubuddhi* and *ahaṅkṛti* belonging to [Name], svāhā" (10); "Oṃ hāṃ, to Sadāśiva, I offer the *manas* belonging to [Name], svāhā" (10). Then: "Oṃ hāṃ guṃ, O Brahmā, accept the portion of the *puryaṣṭaka* belonging to [Name], svāhā" (3).

Oṃ hāṃ guṃ Viṣṇu, accept a portion of the puryaṣṭaka of [Name], svāhā! (3) Oṃ hāṃ guṃ Rudra, accept a portion of the puryaṣṭaka of [Name], svāhā! (3) Oṃ hāṃ guṃ Īśvara, accept a portion of the puryaṣṭaka of [Name], svāhā!
(3) Oṃ hāṃ guṃ Sadāśiva, accept a portion of the puryaṣṭaka of [Name], svāhā! (3) Then follows the full oblation (pūrṇā).
Guṃ bhūrūpabhairavāya vauṣaṭ svāhā. Guṃ, I burn the *karmapāśa* (bond of action) of [Name]’s self; Guṃ phaṭ svāhā phaṭ.
(10) Guṃ, I burn the *māyīyapāśa* (bond of illusion) of [Name]’s self; Guṃ phaṭ svāhā phaṭ. (10) Guṃ, [the bond of] [Name]’s self...

Ṇava-pāśa-dahā-mi-guṃphaṭ svāhā phaṭ (10). Guṃ amuka-ātmanaḥ prāyaścittaṃ śodhayāmi guṃ phaṭ svāhā phaṭ (10). Then the full oblation (pūrṇā): Guṃ amuka-ātmanaḥ prāyaścitta-śuddhiḥ astu svāhā phaṭ. Thereafter, one should offer oblations to Mardaka and the other Kṣetrapālas: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ āmardakāya.
Svāhā! (3) To Kaṅkāla, (0) (3) to Bhīmarāva, (0) (3) to Aṭṭahāsa, (0) (3) to Karavīra, (0) (3) to Karaṅkākhya, (0) (3) to Kāligrāsa, (0) (3) to Kuleśvara, Svāhā! Oṃ hrāṃ kṣaṃ kṣūṃ, svāhā to Heruka!
Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ lāṃ kṣīṃ, [svāhā] to Tripurāntaka! Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ kṣīṃ, [svāhā] to Agnivetāla! Oṃ hrīṃ kṣīṃ hūṃ...
To Agnijihva: Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ kurparāya. To Kāla: Oṃ. To Karāli: Oṃ kṣāṃ yūṃ kṣīṃ. To Ekapāda: Oṃ āṃ yūṃ kṣmīṃ. To Bhīmarūpa: Oṃ kṣāṃ yūṃ kṣāṃ. To Ḍāmara: Oṃ hā. To Ṭaṅkeśvara: Oṃ hā.

Then one should offer oblations to the deities residing in the mind: to Īśāna svāhā, to Rudra svāhā, to Īśvara svāhā, to Viṣṇu svāhā, to Brahmā svāhā, to Indra svāhā, to Yama svāhā, to Soma svāhā, to Apāmpati svāhā, to Carakī svāhā, to Vidhārī svāhā, to Pūtanā svāhā, to Pāparākṣasī svāhā, to Skanda svāhā, to Aryaman svāhā, to Jambuka svāhā, to Pilipiñcha svāhā; and to Śaṅkara svāhā, to Bhava svāhā.

To all Rudras, to Paśupati, to Umāpati, to Skanda, to Bhairava, to the destroyer of fear—svāhā! Now, the dhāraṇā: immediately thereafter, preceded by the utterance of the *praṇava*, having emerged through the right [nostril] and entered the heart of the corpse through the left channel (*vāmanāḍī*), one cuts with the *astra-mantra* the consciousness previously deposited there, draws it out, and [places it] upon that [corpse].

Having exited through the left nostril and entered into the heart of a friend, one should perform the *yojanikā* (the act of union) with the following modification: "Guṃ! I unite the self of [Name], such as Devadatta, in the state of Supreme Śiva—*svāhā*, *vauṣaṭ*. This is done by means of the sequential differentiation of the causal syllables (*kāraṇa-pada*) joined with all the mantras of the mind and vital breath. Then follows the *pūrṇā* (full oblation): "Guṃ! All deficiencies..."
There shall be no addition of *svāhā* or *vauṣaṭ* beyond the prescribed injunctions. Then, one should address the Deity residing within the maṇḍala, the fire, and the water-pot (*kumbha*).

For the purpose of concluding the fire-rite, a flower should be offered into the full fire. Having offered it, one should give the final oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*), especially for those who have been initiated. O Maheśāna, by Your will, there is no transgression of the womb.

O Lord of the World, O God of Gods, O Great Sovereign, O Guru, O Immortal One, since he has been made complete by Your will alone without [further] praise, and since the oblations of the fire-sacrifice have been set in motion by You, grant him this excellent fragrance; may he not take root anywhere again, like a burnt seed.
Grant him the command residing within the fire of the mandala. O Vibhāvasu!

Then, all those who have been initiated should recite and study the *Vidyāvyomeśvarī* seven times with great intensity; by reciting three hundred syllables of this [mantra], the preceptor is liberated and delivered from all sins. When recited even at the edge of the ear, it grants liberation even to bound souls (*paśus*). It should not be spoken of to anyone, whether one desires it or not, nor in a house or a cremation ground, for what reason?

"By the mere utterance of this [mantra], Śiva himself trembles. Thus, one should offer a flower into the fire with: *phaṭ agniṃ vimuñcāmi phaṭ* (3) *nayāmi*. Then, the Vidyā of Vyomīśvarī should be recited over the corpse.
One who has not been initiated should recite this once; one who has been initiated should recite it seven times. In the offering of food (naivedya):
*oṃ haṃsaḥ śuciṣat laṃ vaḥ vyomīśvarī vaṣaṭ saṃ raḥ mahākālasaṅkarṣiṇī vauṣaṭ yaṃ ūṃ vāyvādhāre phaṭ aṃ āṃ īṃ ūṃ yāṃ rāṃ lāṃ māṃ kṣāṃ sarvādhāre*.

Namaḥ to the knower of the Vedas. Ūḥ yaṃ raḥ saṃ vaḥ laṃ saḥ haṃ. To the feet, ankles, shanks, knees, anus, and the Brahma-karaṇeśvarī; to the touch-Haṃsinī, svāhā! To Viśvavahni-Kuṇḍalinī and Viṣṇu-kāraṇeśvarī;
to the touch-Haṃsinī, svāhā! To the lotus-form of the light of the space of the heart...
Haḥ! To the Haṃsī who touches the Lord of the Cause of Rudra within the hollow of the filaments of the lotus, Svāhā!
To the single Gluttonous One (Ghasmarī) who has abandoned the twelve [centers], swallowed the Moon, Sun, and Time, and who touches the Lord of the Cause of Īśvara, Haṃsī, Svāhā!
She who knows the eight skulls, whose forehead-mark is the soundless resonance of the humming of the Sound (Nāda), O Mistress of Sound! Svāhā!
O Goddess Sadāśiva, Sovereign of Causes, who art the Haṃsī touched by the one greedy for the ascent to the supreme ether; Svāhā!

O Sovereign whose form is the manifest supreme light, which has restrained the uneven fires and the bolt of Brahmā’s door beyond the five voids of the ocean of all planets; you who have abandoned the state of being devoid of all volition and the body that transcends the support and the supported.
The swan touches the body; the swan dwells in purity; Svadhā is in the offering. The syllables are three thousand.
Having thus recited the mantra of Vyomeśī seven times with a mind free from conceptualization and fully attentive, one should then utter it just once.
Having placed the fuel upon the consciousness, one should place the corpse upon the consciousness; having brought the Śiva-fire there, [saying] "Phaṭ!
I completely gather the Śiva-fire," one should spread out the sacrificial grass with its tips pointing toward the south and the west.

*Guṃ bahurūpabhairavāya vauṣaṭ svāhā* (108). Then, having performed the full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*), the Guru, holding the *sruk* spoon with its bowl facing upward and the *sruva* ladle with its bowl facing downward, visualizes the head in the form of a cavity within the center of the upturned *sruk*. [He recites: "O Agni, you are the southern time; being brought forth by Time itself, accept this Śaiva offering purified by mantra."

Having loudly recited "mahāhutiṃ svāhā vaṣaṭ uccaiḥ," one should cast the *sruc* and *sruva* ladles right there as they are spoken. Then, upon the burning of the hair, one should snap the fingers over the *astravārdhānī*. Next, having worshipped again at the northeast corner (*īśānakoṇa*), one should worship the weapons for the *aghorāstra* and the *codanāstra*.

Having placed the *astrakarakī* (the weapon-vessel) upon his left shoulder and reciting the *astra-mantra* in the sequence beginning from the north, he should discharge streams [of water] behind him. Reciting the *Aghorāstra-mantra*, "Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ," while remembering Śiva and facing [him], he should again seek forgiveness there in the northeast corner (*īśakoṇa*), recollecting the *samaya*: "Oṃ hūṃ! To the self whose nature is peaceful awakening and light."

Oṃ hāṃ oṃ hīṃ oṃ haiṃ oṃ hauṃ oṃ haḥ oṃ saḥ! O Brahman-self, O embodiment of Brahman, ward off all violations of the observances (samaya); fulfill all the observances; grant your presence! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Having established the deity residing in the fire of the mandala within one's own heart, [one should address him as]: "Oṃ hāṃ, O pure self named so-and-so, always..."

"Śivo bhava svāhā! Oṃ hāṃ, O [Name] of pure self, become peaceful, svāhā! With these words, one should offer three handfuls of sesame seeds and water. Then, one should mutter the Bahurūpa mantra a hundred times; the recitation for the faces is double that amount.
Laṃ, obeisance to the face of Sadyojāta (5). Vaṃ, obeisance to the face of Vāmadeva (4). Raṃ, [obeisance to the face of Aghora...]

For the sake of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, who are marked with the caste-signs of a village-dweller:

Oṃ. Now, on the fourth day, follows the ritual for the collection of bones and the cremation ground. Then, having sprinkled those white [bones] with pure milk, one should cast them into a river; having bathed that spot, one should smear it with cow-dung water.
On its back, having drawn eight lotuses in the shape of *dardaras* with vermilion (*sindūra*), one should place nine vessels upon them and perform worship.

First, one should perform the purification of the seat (*āsana-śuddhi*). *Oṃ*, for this mantra of purifying the venerable seat (*āsana-śodhana-mantra*), Meru-pṛṣṭha is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Pṛthivī is the metre (*chandas*), and the deity is the Lotus-seated One (*kamalāsana*). *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, obeisance to the Support-Power (*ādhāra-śakti*) and to the Lotus-seated One.
"Salutation to the thousand-petaled lotus seat; salutation to the eight-petaled lotus seat. Having thus purified the seat.
One should perform the withdrawal of the elements (*bhūtāpasarpaṇa*). [The removal of] the *arśasarpas* and the *pāṣāṇḍakas*. By three strikes with the heel, those on the earth;
by three claps of the hands, those situated in the intermediate space; by the divine gaze, those in heaven; and by ten snaps of the fingers, [those in] the directions.
